title: Easy to use, with good image quality and lots of options.
text:
This camera replaced my Canon 60D, which now serves as backup. The image quality is excellent, with good, low ISO noise up to ISO 3200, and, with good noise-reduction software, up to 12,800.

Although I bought it for ISO 25,600, where the image quality is adequate with noise reduction, I find its video features very good. Most useful is its ability to autofocus while shooting video. With my 60D, I had to focus manually, or use autofocus in still-picture mode before switching to video. I don't shoot much video, but when I do, I like the capabilities of the 70D.

I can think of three features that might be improved:

1) The camera does three-shot HDR (high dynamic range) by combining three images at different exposures. But to do this, it is necessary to switch from RAW to JPG output in one camera menu, the enable HDR in another menu. The camera could do this automatically. Further, I would like the camera to save one of the three exposures as a RAW or JPG image for me to work with on my computer.

2) The camera has more options for choosing autofocus points than I know what to do with. The 60D was simpler; I could choose any one autofocus point or use all of them merely by turning one dial on the camera. The 70D requires me to push some buttons first.

3) The camera is a bit heavy, but then, so was my 60D. I knew this before buying the camera.

Edited to fix a spelling error.

title: Great protection! Good price! But read on. *UPDATED*
text:
The good: This case provides the best protection for your 2013 Nexus 7. Period. The case actually consists of 2 parts. The hard plastic inside and the rubber cover outside. It's built like a freaking tank. The Nexus now feels invincible against its worst foe: falling. I've dropped it (accidentally, of course) twice from about 3 feet off the ground with the case on. I was amazed when I took the Nexus out of the cover afterwards. Absolutely nothing happened! Still looked like new. The rubber absorbs quite a bit of shock. The remaining force is reduced by the plastic cover. I am very happy pay the $25 to get this kind of protection. The rubber also provides very good grip.
The Nexus fits nicely into the case. The tablet will not move inside the case even if I try to shake it.
The integrated screen cover is useful. However, it has the rainbow effect. I don't really mind this, just letting you know. Read on for the real cons of the cover.
A big plus for this case is the stand. This thing is genius! Whoever thought of it deserves a huge raise. I found that I could use the stand in FOUR different ways, giving me four different viewing angles. The symbol on the stand looks cool. I don't know what it stands for, but it's cool, so hey! Read on for cons also.
The cutouts are well placed. There are even cutouts for speakers. There are covers for the audio jack and the USB port. I don't see the need for these covers, but they sure look good, are well designed and do their job well.
The buttons for the power and volume are very responsive. No problem pressing any of those buttons at all.

The bad: The integrated cover has the rainbow effect. I didn't subtract any points for this. Also, there are plastic covers on BOTH sides of this cover when you first get it. So be sure to remove them before posting any negative comments on how it has scratches.
The problem with the cover is that it makes the touch screen unresponsive occasionally. I was somewhat frustrated with this. I would need to press several times to get the touch to register. Note that this doesn't happen all that often. I actually used an app to test the touch screen with this cover. Most of the time, the touch will register fine. Multi-touch works fine too. But the occasional unresponsiveness was enough for me to remove the cover all together. Yes, I removed the integrated cover. This might come back and bite me if I manage to get something to scratch the screen. So I plan to apply a separate screen cover on later. I will update if I do. This is a minor problem so I only subtracted half a star for this.
Another problem is with the stand. Sure, it might be the best stand I've ever seen (More covers should use this design), but the built quality isn't up to my expectations. Specifically, the bolts in the hinges could actually become loose and run off if you don't pay close attention. One example is the bolt in the hinge between that foldable metal thing and the stand itself. Mine completely came out. Luckily, I caught it red handed trying to escape. So with some imagination and a tiny bit of super glue, I VERY carefully glued the bolt permanently inside the hinge. I took care not to glue the hinge itself. That would be very, very bad. I think I did a fine job. The bolt now stays in the hinge. The stand still opens and closes like usual. However, no one should have to do this. So I subtracted half a star for this. The other bolts also had similar problems, but they are more cowardly, so they don't move that much. I don't think they'll run off to anywhere soon, especially after the first escapee had been made an example of. However, only time will tell.

The meh: The cover adds quite a lot of weight to the tablet. I expected it this, so I didn't subtract anything, just be aware of this.
The rubber is surprisingly not much of a dust magnet thanks to the somewhat rough surface, but it still attracts some dust.

Overall: Want protection? Get this! Want a functional stand? Get this! These two alone is worth the $25 you pay. You might want to buy a separate screen cover to replace the integrated cover, but it's up to you. Pay close attention to the bolts. One warning sign is that the cover will not fold nicely into its original place because of the bolts, so if you notice this, be aware of potential escapes.

UPDATE: 04/05/14: Upgraded to 5 stars for excellent customer service and improved integrated cover

So the hinge between the metal thing and the stand broke off rendering the stand useless. So I emailed their customer service to claim the warranty. After 3 email exchanges, I provided them with the invoice, photo of the damaged case, confirmation of my address. They responded to my emails quickly. And they mailed me a whole new case immediately! Now, THAT's what customer service should be. So for the price, I would definitely recommend the case and the company. You won't be disappointed.

Now I think they've taken the feedback about the integrated cover and improved it. I'm not 100% sure if they did because I threw my cover out previously so there's nothing to compare. But there's no rainbow effect now. And the touch feedback has been registering fine. I would have to wait to see the durability of the stand. But as of now, this case is a 5 five star product.

EDIT: Well, there was a protective layer behind the cover, so after I removed this, the rainbow effect is back. Not worth taking anything off though. The touch still works fine after all.

title: I *REALLY* like this case  - and the customer service is great!
text:
Update 1/09/2013

I received the replacement case from Florence and everything lines up perfectly now. I'm bumping this case up to 5 stars because the more I used it, the more I really started to like it.

Issues #1, 2 and 3 were all resolved with the new case. It fits much better. #4 really isn't much of an issue anymore, either - you get used to it quite quickly. Even the poorly coded apps that don't auto-rotate properly, you get used to using the case so they are right side up.

Customer service was also a pleasure to deal with. Florence shipped me out a new case and a prepaid envelope to return the defective one. It's very nice that I didn't have to return it first and have an unprotected Kindle. Thanks Florence!

I bought 2 cases for my Kindle Fire HD 7". This rooCASE Origami, and the Moko 360 degree rotating case. I really like the feeling of the pleather on this rooCASE, but I ran into an issue immediately after putting my kindle in.

#1 The cutouts for the microphone, microUSB, and miniHDMI ports were not lined up too well. The microphone was completely covered by the case. The microUSB I needed to pull and stretch to get the cable to go in, and the speakers aren't really all that open either.

#2 I may have received a defective case, but the magnets did not hold all that well - the stand is "OK" the Moko stand is 100 times better, but it doesn't have the nice feeling in your hand that this rooCASE has. This case feels more solid, but the stand positions are flimsy - especially when the magnet is coming unattached.

#3 the part of leather that was on the camera side was raised up quite a bit and not flush with the kindle- this may have been a manufacturing defect.

#4 The fact that the kindle opens backwards (depending on what country you're from and what language you read) really irks me. When you open the case from right to left the camera is on the right side and the volume and power buttons are on the bottom. The proper way is to have the camera on the left and the buttons on the top. However, in order to achieve this, you need to open the case from left to right which is super awkward. Not only that, but not all apps are coded to rotate 360 degrees (certain games and streaming apps) - so when you open it like you would a book, it's upside down. :\

Aside from all that - it is a really solid material and while it adds some bulk to the kindle - that's good in my case. Unfortunately I think for now I will be sticking with the Moko.

text:
If you've read reviews regarding the ZT60, you already know the black levels are great, the picture is no better in a dark room than the VT60, it is better than the VT60 in a bright room, and the Samsung F8500 is brighter than the VT and ZT (blacks not as good as Panasonic though), the speakers are not the greatest and it's expensive. So, maybe it's time for a subjective review.
We moved up from a 50 inch Panasonic that is about 6 years old. Subjectively, for what it's worth, this is a gorgeous television. Couple it with a nice home theater receiver like the Denon X4000, a nice center channel (after all, most of your sound comes from the center channel, and good quality front and surround speakers, and you have a system that will put you in home theater heaven for the next 10 years.
Yes, you can nitpick the products in comparison to death. But, Panasonic has always made a great plasma television. For my money, again subjectively, I would never purchase an LED tv. Black levels are just so important and I've yet to see an LED with great black levels. Of course, I haven't seen them all.
All I really know is what my eyes tell me. Since getting the ZT60 they've been telling me "nice decision".
I did not buy this from Amazon. I bought it from Magnolia (Best Buy). I really appreciate the Magnolia stores because they cater to customers interested in higher quality audio and visual gear. Prices are fair, the salesman (Richfield, MN) was knowledgeable, the installers were pleasant and competent. Not necessarily what you've come to expect in the past from Best Buy. Magnolia of course is a separate store within selected Best Buy stores.
This stuff is not cheap folks! Because of the expense, we as consumers would like to "future proof" our AV investment as best we can. If you have the money, shop wisely, don't cut corners, and build a great home theater system. Otherwise, you buy lower end brands in the name of saving money, with disappointing results, and just have to replace the stuff in a relatively short period of time.
Lastly, it is absolutely impossible to judge the quality of a television picture in any showroom. You just need to trust fellow reviewers, buy the best equipment you can afford, and enjoy!

However, the company needs a major rewrite of the manual, or at least a helpful troubleshooting section.

Please consider the following before buying:

1. If your LAN subnet is NOT 192.168.1.x, it will be painful to configure it. My LAN subnet is 192.168.0.x. This device has a default IP of 192.168.1.66 and I couldn't communicate to it. The manual says to put your PC on the same subnet: 192.168.1.x. However, if your router uses a different LAN subnet, it wouldn't allow a 192.168.1.x IP address to communicate.

I am a technical person, and luckily I had a network switch. I was able to connect my laptop with a 192.168.1.x address to this switch, then change change nus2000's configuration to have an IP in my LAN subnet: 192.168.0.66.

I can't believe this device has a hardcoded IP address and does not detect and auto-configure an IP in the local subnet. In any case, please ensure you will be able to get to 192.168.1.66 IP address easily per your router settings. Although many routers do have 192.168.1.x IP range as LAN, there are many that do not. (Unless you are using AirPort; per the manual this device has a way to get around its 10.x IP scheme. I haven't tried Mac AirPort setup).

2. This device does NOT have NFS. It was an assumption on my part since it says "network storage." I spent a while trying to configure my NFS client on Linux but realized later the NUS2000 does not support it.

3. I was able to use WebDav, ONLY after changing the password scheme to "Basic," by default its set to "Digest," however extra configuration is needed on the client side to enable this. The manual should be clearer about this. I kept getting "authorization errors" until I changed to Basic mode (Note: do NOT use "Basic" Auth mode for WebDAV on an unsecured wireless network, the password is sent over plaintext and could be sniffed).

Bottom line: unless you home network is setup just they way the product designers imagined, it may be difficult to get it up and running. However, once you do, it provides a good service at a low cost compared to other alternatives.

title: Slow writes; Software less than worthless; But can be a good value
text:
Performance:
------------
Writing speed is a slow 4 MB/sec. Reading is a respectable (adequate) 20 MB/sec. This was tested transferring a 4 GB file -- the drive comes formatted as FAT32 and this is its maximum file size. For reference, reading a similar file from a USB 2.0 external hard drive tends to be about 30 MB/sec.

This product can be a good value for a number of the common uses of flash drives. For example, it may be a mirror for large portions of your laptop for those occasions where you didn't anticipate needing the laptop and the cloud isn't a practical alternative. In such cases, although the contents of the flash drive can be large, the amount of change at any one time tends to be small, so the slow write speed is not a real inconvenience.
Caveat on "value": what is a good value one day (or hour) may not be such the next.

Construction:
-------------
The plastic case _feels_ flimsy because it flexes easily, but it does _not_ display some of the other characteristics of materials that would break easily. This concern about how rugged it actually is will limit when and how I carry it.

Operation of the retractable connector: Good. It locked into the extended position reliably, and the unlock tab is big and easy to operate. However, if you are inserting this into a tight space, it doesn't take much of a bump on that tab to unlock it. I see this only as an inconvenience to those whose only available USB ports are in out-of-the way locations.

The hole for the lanyard is unusually large: over 1/4-inch across. The crossbar is thicker than that on most of the flash drives I see: it is almost 1/16-inch thick.

Included Software: Junk
-----------------------
1. SanDisk Secure Access: I am inclined to describe this a primarily Ad-ware rather than functional software. The "vault" is incredibly primitive: It is simply a partition that holds encrypted versions of your files. To update a file, you use the primitive UI to manually take it out of the vault, edit it, and put it back into the vault. When much of the information that you would likely want to put into the vault is subject to periodic updating, this is both tedious and error-prone. At the very _minimum_ you want to have the ability to record the location of the master copy of the files as part of the meta-data in the vault and have the vault's software alert you when a pairing is out-of-sync. And the vault software should not be installed on your computer because that opens the door to multiple sources of inadvertent and malicious errors. SanDisk Secure Access delivers none of what I consider to be the basics for such software, and there are better alternatives available targeted at different needs and levels of sophistication.
ADVICE: If you decide to try this in a version of Windows that has the Restore Point feature, create one so that you can roll back to it rather than having to trust the software's own uninstall process. When software has a large Ad-ware component, I find it wise to be paranoid.

2. "Club SanDisk" included software: "GoToMyPC", "RoboForm Password Manager", "McAfee Internet Security Software" and "IE8 Sidebar for eBay". I wasn't interested in any of these and didn't try them. The sidebar was described as "a free tool" and the others are presumably the trials or "lite" editions common to such offerings.

-- Douglas B. Moran

I will say that the included desk stand supports my dual 24" monitors in a stable position the way I have it adjusted. However, if both arms are extended all the way out front, the whole thing will tip forward. And you could always use the included hardware to drill into your desk for what I assume would be a more stable (and permanent) setup. I will say that the sound with my iPod is very good. Great clarity in the mid-range and upper frequencies, but not as punchy in the bass as I would like. I've owned several sets of in-ear headphones and know the value of a proper fit in the ear canal (this is not the problem). I suspect that drivers in the Shure SE425s require a bit more power than my iPod can dish out.

All in all, I'm very satisfied with the SE 425s.

Update - Feb 24, 2012: After using these for a few weeks they have definitely opened up. The bass is much better when playing through my iPod/iPhone. I'm very happy with these!

title: Display Too Dim for Daytime Use
text:
I ordered the nuvi 65 to replace a nuvi 1450 that was damaged on a trip. The 1450 has been great for us but lacked map updates and had a poor touch screen.

We found that the nuvi 65 screen is almost unusable in our cars on a sunny day while wearing sunglasses. We tried various brightness setting and even switched to night mode, which makes some text a little easier to read. My wife had even more trouble reading the display than I did. I don't know why other reviewers haven't described this problem.

After talking with Garmin customer service (very polite) I exchanged the unit through Amazon. The second unit was identical, so I figured the problem was not a fluke. A visit to Best Buy revealed that all of the new Garmins seem to have this new type of display with less contrast and/or brightness as well as graphics with less contrast. The displays look fine indoors but comparing the new units to older (nuvi 50, dezl 760) units on their shelf, the problem is clearly across the new line. We returned the second unit and have ordered a nuvi 2555 and have our fingers crossed.

I'm disappointed because otherwise, the 65 had many advantages. I liked the new display of the street you are currently on at the bottom of the screen. The nuvi 65 has a much better touch screen than the 1450. I really liked the new split-screen display, particularly with the bigger 6" display. I preferred the 1450's odd state, city, street address entry method over the new one, but I think with some experimentation the new method might have been just as good. (I disliked the 1450 method until I noted the street name search advantages.) I also missed the option of displaying several data options on the main screen at once (elevation, arrival time, etc.) but on balance I still liked the 65 more than the 1450. I hope the display problem will be solved so I can buy a nuvi 65 in the future, but as is, it would be useless to us during the day. I really would have liked the larger display if it was just as bright and clear.

Update: The map themes didn't seem to help our viewing problem much and the polarization suggestion didn't seem to help, but last year my daughter needed a navigator and the nuvi 65 met her needs best, so we tried again. The one she received has a perfectly good display that works well in all lighting. I don't know if Garmin changed the displays, the drivers, or if there is a lot of variation between units.

title: Heavily modified version of Android may be annoying to some
text:
This is a basic review of the Kindle Fire HD 7". It is not a detailed review and is more about an issue with the modified version of Android that the Kindle runs on. If you don't care about the operating system or user interface then this review probably won't be helpful to you.

I have had the Kindle FIre HD 7" for a little over 3 months now. It has held up well and I have not had any major issues with it. It is fast and responsive and the display is clear bright and crisp.

My only major issue is with the Kindle FIre is the modified version of Android that it uses. It is not anything like what you'd expect from the typical Android setup. The user interface is easy to navigate and is straight-forward, but it seems like you're navigating through a cheap mobile web store. You can't even change the background so if you like the customization and freedom that comes with most Android OS' then you will be disappointed. It lacks basic features of the typical Android environment. Furthermore, the Kindle Fire is not compatible with a lot of apps that other devices are compatible with. The appstore is more filtered than Google Play. Do not expect to be able to download Google Play to get your apps from there. You have to use the Amazon Appstore for your apps. Overall the OS takes away a lot of the freedoms and features of the Android environment such as text-to-speech options, extensive settings menus, and wide ranging app compatibility.

Overall: The Kindle Fire HD is a great option for those who are new to tablets/ touch screen devices. The device itself is speedy and has a good display and is overall pretty solid. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a cheap reliable tablet. However, if you are expecting the version of Android to be similar to other versions, you will be disappointed. There are other similarly priced tablets that run less modified versions of Android that are probably just as good as the Kindle.

title: My Chromebook Review, or, Life in the Clouds
text:
I will say it very directly: this device is of superb quality, especially considering the price. You can see the specs above these reviews (where amazon usually lists them), so I won't cover that. Rather, I will cover those things that make this device an OUTSTANDING value for the price.

First, let's just go with the Chromebook concept, which some like and others dislike. I love the idea largely because every computer I've owned, since it has a lot of software, takes a long time to boot, gets progressively slower with each new download or install, and requires periodic maintenance to de-clutter. Not so with this: it boots in 10 or fewer seconds, and since there is no software on the device except for the small OS (a file manager and a web browser, really), you don't have to worry about your computer slowing down. And for those who want software on their device, ask yourself (as I asked myself): how much time do you really do stuff offline? IF you didn't have an internet connection, how much time would you really spend using your computer? And if still unconvinced, ask yourself whether the trade-off of a slower, heavier, and energy-sucking computer is h it to you.

Now what about this Chromebook. Well, it beats the [[ASIN:B009LL9VDG Samsung Chromebook (Wi-Fi, 11.6-Inch)]] in a few ways: connectivity, screen, and keyboard. (It is SLIGHTLY lighter at 2.2 rather than 2.6 pounds, but I don't see that as a huge advantage.) The screen is brighter, and while it is not the matte screen of the Samsung, the trade-off is that the screen is brighter (the matte seemed to dull the color a bit).

The keyboard is easily - EASILY - the best small-device keyboard I've typed on; while the Samsung was good, this keyboard is a bit "springier" and responsive in a tactile way. (I used to have a netbook way back yonder, and the keyboard was positively awful. This review is being typed on my HP Chromebook, and I have not experienced anywhere near THAT level of frustration.) The only thing that is hard to get used to is the lack of "function" keys and, more importantly, the lack of a caps lock key (which is now a 'search' key that pulls up your app list.)

Connectivity? Well, let's just say that my Samsung had serious connectivity issues. While it was most probably a defective unit, any google search of "Samsung Chromebook connectivity issues" will quickly show you that MANY other people have the same problem. This device, so far, has always found my wi-fi signal, never kicked me off of it, and 'holds onto' even relatively weak wi-fi signals.

The last thing worth mentioning about this device is that it is just darn nice looking. I have the white device with blue 'highlights' (the 'highlights' are on a rubberized bottom, perfect for keeping the device secure on a desk, and a little tasteful 'ring' around the keyboard.) The device, like the Samsung, is made of plastics, but it absolutely does not feel cheap. Instead, it is very solid in the hands and just feels great to pick up, especially compared to my 'regular' clunker of a laptop.

Long and short, if you at all like the idea of a Chromebook - and as a second device, it does everything most people would need it to do INCLUDING offline google docs and gmail editing - this is the device you should consider. There is a 14 inch model that has a better battery life (advertised as eight hours, where this one is about six), but it is a bit more expensive and quite a bit heavier. I am sold on the idea of a Chromebook, and so far, this is a purchase I absolutely do not regret.

text:
Fits my Philips Fidelio X1 well, with only very minor movement in any direction. The cable must be removed, which is completely understandable, but I have to directly challenge their claim that "it can hold a bunch of gear": The accessory pouch is only big enough to fit an adapter and a small portable amp/DAC, and It's zippered in the center, making even an E07K awkward to get in and out. The cable just has to be laid under or on top of the cans. Sure, technically you could fit a large set of headphones, the cable, a portable amp/DAC, and its cable, but you won't like doing it. The simple solution is a full width, elastic mesh pouch in one of the halves. This would have the side effect of stabilizing the headphones, which brings me to my next point...

The "padding" is just felt lining, so if your headphones don't exactly fill the void (fortunately mine do), the case will only protect against scuffs and scratches, not bumps and shakes. For the price, I would like to have seen a bit of neoprene or foam cushioning as a shock absorber, at least. The location of the strap certainly doesn't help things, either, making the case into a big pendulum if you tried to actually carry it that way.

When you get right down to it, this isn't much more than a container shaped for headphones. This case is great if you only want to put your headphones away on a shelf when they aren't being used, but you could do just as well with a felt bag. For any sort of actual protection or storage, you're going to want something more substantial.

title: Save your money if you don't have a recent camera body
text:
I've done some write benchmarks on the 16GB version of this card and others with my Canon 40D. Here are the results:

SanDisk Extreme 60 MB/s 16GB (400X)
17 RAW, 17 seconds to clear

SanDisk Extreme III 30 MB/s 8GB (200X)
18 RAW, 17 seconds to clear

Lexar Pro 1GB 133X
20 RAW, 16 seconds to clear

Kingston Ultimate 4 GB 133X
19 RAW, 21 seconds to clear

Kingston High Speed 1024 MB 80X
18 RAW, 37 seconds to clear

For this circa-2007 DSLR, no card over 133X improves write speeds. No benefit was expected; cameras of this vintage max out at about 12 MB/s.

For more recent bodies, head directly to Rob Galbraith's CF/SD/XQD database. He's tested every significant Canon and Nikon camera since October 2008, starting with Canon's 50D and Nikon's D90, with every significant memory card.

* A few general notes:

There are speed variances even among cards of equal rating. Brand matters. Cameras from Canon, Nikon, and Sony perform best with cards from SanDisk and Lexar. Other brands, even if capable of rated speed in a card reader, tend not to rival those two in-camera.

Card-to-computer transfer rates will be limited by the card reader interface or the camera. Most cameras directly connected to a computer send data at 10-15 MB/s. With card readers, USB 2.0, the most common interface, caps out at about 30 MB/s. Firewire 800 is about three times as fast and will max out this card, as will USB 3.0 and IDE/SATA converters. As well, all CF cards rated for 30 MB/s or more support UDMA.

* Are higher-rated cards faster?

Autofocus, turn-on speed, JPEG writes, movie recording, image review, maximum framerate, and so on are almost completely unaffected by faster cards. Movie recording at 1080p/30 takes just 5-10 MB/s. The sole benefit to a higher rating with a modern camera is reduced buffer clearing time with continuous high-speed raw. Put another way, the card speed only matters after you've banged off those first 20 raw shots at 6-8 fps. I have to list a caveat for certain older bodies; Sony's A850 and A350 from 2009 and 2008, and perhaps other DSLRS not from Canon or Nikon, will have delayed image review with slow cards.

Raw throughput is limited by the camera's processing hardware. Through 2008, most DSLRs maxed out under 15 MB/s. From 2008 to 2011, all but Canon's 7D and 1D IV peaked at around 35 MB/s (e.g., Canon 50D, Canon 5D II, Nikon D300, Nikon D3). Now in 2012, a number of cameras (e.g., Nikon D800, Nikon D4, Canon 1D X, Canon 5D III) reach 70 MB/s or more.

Cards faster than the camera's processing hardware may perform better, but not in proportion to their rating. Canon's 7D manages 24/41/58 MB/s with 200/400/1000X cards, respectively. The same cards with Nikon's D3S yield 24/36/42 MB/s. These diminishing returns apply doubly with SD-based cameras. Nikon's D7000 only writes 20% faster with a 650X card over a 200X card.

Unless you're riding right on the edge of the camera's raw buffer with continuous shooting, you'll never notice these differences. This 60 MB/s (400X) card is for you if you have a recent semi-professional or professional body and regularly hit a buffer limit in raw, or you shoot so much with any camera that card-to-computer times slow your workflow. Everyone else can spend less on the 30 MB/s (200X) version of same.

Please leave a comment if you intend to downvote, I do try to be accurate and I'd much rather know the issue.

title: SoundLink III a worthy successor to the previous SoundLink series.
text:
Keeping with the tradition of the SoundLink series, the SoundLink III is a worthy follow-on to the SoundLink II. It is hard to believe the room-filling sound such a small speaker can produce. Bass is accurate and sharp, highs are true to the instruments, and vocals are superb.

Some have mentioned that a USB charging interface would be more convenient. The problem is that the Bose has a large, powerful battery, which requires 18V to charge, and hence, a larger power supply. The USB standard is 5V at 2 amps, or 10 watts. I would estimate a minimum of 2 days to charge this with USB, assuming a step-up transformer could bring the input voltage up.

I own the SoundLink II and Mini SoundLink, and must say this is their best offering so far. The Mini is great for smaller spaces, and the SoundLink II and III fill larger rooms, and are also ideal for outdoor use.

title: Outstanding Quality for a Compact Unit
text:
I have had the G-17 for a month now, and I'm extremely pleased with its design and function. As an audiophile, I find the sound quality, including bass, to be outstanding for its small size, and the output is fine for a large bedroom, where it resides. An iPad supplies the input, utilizing Apple Lossless files. I had a small amount of difficulty in the setup using the supplied iPad app, which was quickly and easily corrected by contacting Klipsch. I have an Airport Express in the room for signal boost, which seems to almost completely avoid the occasional very short signal drop-offs that occur. Of course, it's hard to tell if the iPad or G-17 is responsible for these. I suspect the iPad, as they usually occur when opening other programs while listening to music. I think that the poor volume output that some people have experienced may be related to the files that they are listening to, as I have found that the inherent sound level of my various lossless tracks/albums can vary greatly, a situation that is easily corrected with the volume control on the iPad or with the remote supplied with the unit.

Overall, I think that while this unit is at the upper end of the price range for this type of product, its sound quality is significantly better than that of competing brands. And of course, that is why you would buy a high-end audio product.

title: Nice, High Quality Cable

title: Excellent case and excellent price!
text:
I bought this case to replace a more expensive one I bought for my Kindle Fire HDX 7 inch tablet that didn't have the auto wake-up feature and was too thin and floppy for my taste. I also didn't like the fact that, on some apps, the original case had me holding my Fire upside down - but that actually appears to be a problem with the way the device is designed and not the cases. Oh well...not the hill I want to die on.

This case is great. I love the blue color (kind of like a deep swimming pool blue...darker than the image in the description, which looks like light blue to me). It does have the auto wake-up/sleep feature which is very convenient. I hated having to put my Fire to sleep manually with the other case.

The inside left cover is actually quite impressive: two credit card slots, a small slot for what might hold an SD card or thumb drive, and a hand strap for extra security. The back of the case has cut outs for the power button, volume buttons, and speakers - which is great, because I didn't think this case had holes for the speakers.

The case also came with a handy pen/stylus in a silver finish. It feels quite cheap when you hold it, but it works great. There's an elastic loop on the outside of the case to hold the stylus.

I wish the Kindle folks hadn't designed the device to be upside down for certain apps (for example, a white noise app I have doesn't flip both ways...so when I open the case as it should be and turn on the app, I have to flip the Fire around to use the app. Annoying.) It's the device that's designed this way, though, so there's not much the case makers can do. Most importantly, when I read books and magazines on my Fire, the case is the right way...so that's really all that matters to me.

This case is totally a keeper...and I think the price was a great deal ($4.95 with $4.98 shipping). Oh and shipping time was just ok. I ordered it on October 19th and received it on October 26th. Not bad in general, I guess, but I'm a bit spoiled by Amazon Prime 2 day shipping. :-) Regardless, I'm very happy with the case and would definitely buy from this seller again. Thanks!

title: Simply Awesome!
text: I bought this about almost 9 months ago here on amazon and it has worked like a charm ever since. I have polk audio speakers in my car and this bazooka tube compliments them so well. This sub really adds back the bass that goes missing when you upgrade your factory speakers and it is perfect for my small car. This sub can get extremely loud for only being 100watts, so if you have a small vehicle ie: nissan versa, chevy sonic, ford focus sized vehicle this will be perfect! To hook it up I also bought the bazooka universal wiring harness (Bazooka FAST-9999 Fast Universal Harness) , which worked out perfectly, you just match up and attach the wires to the same color on your car stereo. The only thing that you need to make sure that you do correctly is ground the sub. it needs to touch actual metal, no paint can be on it. Without the ground wire the speaker will not turn on at all. So if you have symtoms of it not working but you can't figure out why, check the ground wire and make sure it is touching straight metal. Also picked up the extension cable to run it from my trunk to the front head unit (Bazooka FAST-BTAH Fast Extension Cable). Very satisfied.

title: Not the most durable
text: I own several of these devices for my vehicles at work.  The batteries to these units specifically state "do not expose to temps above 140" and yet the interior of vehicles routinely exceed that in the summer.  I've had a number of batteries swell up and stop working.  I cannot find replacements.  My AT&T rep helps me out when he can, but overall, I'm not impressed with these.  When I look up the website for more info, they talk about all the new updates circa 2011.  I'm not sure if this company is still producing this particular unit, but they do support it on the web through real time tracking.  The connections are hard wired into the dash, and the connection to the unit itself becomes dislodged at times, requiring a revisit by the install tech.  This disconnect takes place where the unit is plugged into the cord, which is by design.  There is no hard wire connect into the unit itself.  Only from the units power cord to your vehicle.  I would probably give this a 5 out 10 rating.  I'm looking for something more reliable and possibly less expensive to operate, but in the meantime I'm using what I have 5 operating units and 2 broken ones.

title: Fantastic 'phones
text:
Using this only for computer audio listening. Plugged into Audioquest Dragonfly, the sound is very detailed and balanced, with no overemphasis anywhere in the audioband. Very good sound quality. Even lowly MP3s (256 and 384 kbps) sound great. With lossless rips from CD, I have not heard other phones for the price that are better with the Dragonfly. Earcups and the 'phones overall are supremely comfortable and provide good isolation on planes/in airports.

Honestly, the Dragonfly/M4U 1 combo is so good, I find it hard to pick a winner between this and my "real" headphone setup (AKG K701 with Violectric HPA V100 headphone amp) when playing the same source material. Although the AKGs are even more comfortable to me and just may sound a bit "airier" (they're open-back, after all). But with the recent pricedrop on the Dragonfly (sells for $200 now), the Dragonfly/M4U 1 combo costs about a quarter of what the AKG/Violectric set me back (once the Cambridge DacMagic and interconnects needed for the latter combo are factored in).

Also, these are sensitive enough to be driven directly (w/o portable headphone amp) sufficiently loudly by my HTC Amaze and Nexus 7 (2013), though volume levels on both devices are basically almost (HTC) or fully (Nexus) turned up.

title: Endearing Device with an Achilles Heel
text:
Great device - fits in hip pocket of slacks, web access is great, marvelous device for everything from book reading to magazines to video to casual game play.

BUT...

My second unit (warranty replacement for the first) is going back for the same problem - failure of the charging port.

The micro-USB port design used on this device is anything but robust - it should last a lot longer than five months. Motorola manages this on their phones with a much more robust design. And, given the thickness of this device, the designer could go to mini-USB, which is much more mechanically robust.

If this one fails out of warranty, the replacement is going to be a tablet with a more robust power connection. I hate the thought of anything Apple, but their magnetic power supply connection is looking mighty attractive about now.

title: So much potential, so little consistency
text:
I bought a pack of this film to use in a Spectra camera I got off of eBay. All of my prints have poor color balance. Sometimes the prints lack contrast. Sometimes they lack saturation. I have had prints that were tined brown and others are tinted blue. The performance of my film pack is very inconsistent. Do your research you'll see that this is a common complaint about the film.

Others may disagree and I can see why. There are scans available on Flickr and other photo site of beautiful shots with wonderful color tones and contrast. Maybe they got lucky with their combination of film and camera.

My problems could be due to the camera. Perhaps the rollers aren't spreading the developer properly.

Cost is also an issue. Each print is about $3. That's an expensive mistake if your shot is over or under exposed. I am surprised that the batteries of today are so much thicker than yesteryear that the pack loses two shots. If Impossible does thin out the battery and add two more shots I doubt they will lower the price. Overall this film should cost half of what it does today.

I am surprised that with so much technology at our disposal Impossible cannot produce a consistently performing film. Perhaps Edwin Land really did take his secret formula to the grave. Maybe the technology is locked up in patents. Hopefully Impossible will figure things out and update their film here.

title: You are paying for three good stands and tote all other things come for free
text:
The price that you are paying for this thing is just insane. With that said you are basically paying for two good metal 7" stands and a 3-4" front metal front stand. The bulbs, Tote, and sockets you can say they throw it for free.

Mine came perfectly wrapped, on time and with out any missing parts. This is a beginners set so people expecting professional quality for $49 are just plain mad for $49 you cannot get even a professional Bulb. This is excellent set for a basic three point lighting kit. if you want to know about three point lightning go here:

[...]

Some recommendations before using this. 1. Don't trash the boxes that come within the tote it helps you to handle and storage all the equipment better and keep it protected from scratches etc. With the boxes you can put all those things back in the tote easily.
2. DO NOT FORCE THE KNOTS AND BOLTS to keep the lights/umbrellas on place they are made of plastic and will break be gentle with them or they will break. the parts are made of plastic and very light so you don't need that much force.

The positives
1. Great stands that cost much more than $49.
2. Excellent set for a basic three point lightning.
3. Cables are long and have enough length to run around a small room. (what this lights are for)

Neutral
1. Some people complained about the lights not being powerful enough. With that concern I went to Home Depot and spent $10 getting two 75 watt day light bulbs, they spread light about the same amount than the lights that come with the set. For a small setting these lights are bright enough.
2. Tote. if you keep your boxes then you can put everything back inside with ease. Do not force the zipper and it will last and make very easy to transport the equipment, it is not the strongest tote ever but it does it's job.

Not so good:
1. Well for $49 you can't complain that much but al the bolts and knobs to tight the lights sockets, umbrellas, etc. are made of plastic. if you try to tighten them too hard they will break, they are plastic! just be careful (you don't need to tight these things too hard)
2. Umbrellas seem cheap but they do the job of diffusing the light and not shoot it directly to the subject creating that "deer spooked by a headlight" effect.

This is an indoor, studio type, lightning set. it was not made for outdoor use.it will improve dramatically the quality of your photos/video in low light conditions like living rooms, kitchens, media rooms, etc.

Don't spend thousands of dollars on a camera that captures low light conditions instead spend $49 and get this and keep that budget camera in use.

title: These 'phones are a knockout!
text:
So, I've had these headphones for about 30 days now. Truthfully, I had fallen in love with these after only a couple of hours of listening to them. For me, that's a really big deal; because prior to these SL300s, I tried the SOL Republic Tracks, the Creative WP-350s, and even the Soul by Ludacris SL150s. They were all fantastic in their own respective ways, but I couldn't stand to have any of them on my ears for more than an hour. These SL300s are the exception.

Pretty much, everyone before me has commented on how great they sound. These headphones do sound amazing. You can listen to them with the noise-cancelling on or off (powered or non-powered). Like other reviewers have mentioned, these sound their absolute best with the noise-cancelling feature turned on, as every sound in the frequency range that these 'phones can produce is amplified. To achieve that same effect and fullness of sound with the noise-cancelling turned-off will require significantly more volume from the output source. Still, these 300s are huge headphones and will probably completely cover most peoples' ears. Noise-cancelling is excellent, and even when powered-off, their noise-isolation capabilities are pretty good.

The SL300s are nicely-packaged, and come with lots of additional accessories that add value to the product. Having a choice of 2 different audio cables expands the possibilities for how I can use these 'phones. I do not own an Apple product, and my Android phone is extremely selective when it comes to mobile headsets. So, I can use the deleted in-line control cable, instead. This cable option allows me to use the 300s with pretty much every portable device I have. The other cable with the in-line controller on it is exclusively for Apple devices, but the play/pause/answer/end/mute button may work on select Android devices. Also, I really appreciate the fact that the 300s are foldable, and come supplied with a hard travel case. It even has a D-ring on it, so that you can clip it to your backpack. The included polishing cloth is a nice touch, but I probably won't ever use it.

The 300s were supplied with a set of 2 AAA batteries. I got about 25-30 hours of use from them, before replacing with a fresh set. I never got them to the point where the power indicator started flashing, but I felt like the sound was lacking, so I replaced them anyway. The "illuminating logo" feature that these 'phones have is incredibly cool, and makes for a nice "halo" effect when worn at night, or in dark places. I really, really like this feature.

There's a whole lot of good that I can say about these 'phones. I can't think of anything bad to say about them, except that they're gigantic and probably shouldn't be worn outside. I would hate to have them knocked-off my head just to fall onto concrete pavement. Still, these are incredible headphones, and I don't feel the least bit guilty for buying them. I hope that my review helps you in your quest for finding an affordable entry into pure audio bliss. Good luck, and jam out!

title: Complex setup and poor sound
text:
I was looking for a 2.1 Home Theater system and I picked this system simply because of the ability to setup the speakers as towers. Setup isn't simple, as you will have to unpack the contents from multiple layers of styrofoam trays. You will need a screwdriver regardless of whether you will set the system up as towers or as a soundbar, as the bases for either setup have to be screwed on. As other reviewers have stated, the wireless aspect of the "Wireless Subwoofer" is really just that the link between the speakers and subwoofer is a wireless connection. Otherwise, you still have to run two power cables: one for the speakers and one for the subwoofer. If you are doing a soundbar setup, no additional wires are needed. For the tower setup, you will have to run a wire between the two towers in addition to the power cord. HDMI and/or optical cables are all run to the subwoofer. Once setup, the system turned on and connected to my sources and TV perfectly. The "Anynet" feature is neat in that you can control the sound system volume and on/off function through your TV, but you will need to have the TV connected to the system using an HDMI cable for this to work.

In regards to the sound quality: it is awful. I found the sound to be muddled, as the mids and vocals were not clear and distinct. They were drowned out by high background music in movies. Playing with the sound modes did yield noticeable differences, but did not help to produce quality sound. I would have to turn up the system to hear dialogue that when background music started playing, it would come out too loud and require me to turn the volume down. I ended up testing the system setup in both the towers as well as the soundbar, but there was no difference in sound quality (not that I expected any, but I tried for the heck of it).

I was disappointed enough in the sound quality of the system that I ended up returning the system and exchanging it for a Sony CT-150. The Sony is a standard soundbar and not the towers I wanted, but the Sony's sound quality is drastically better than this Samsung's. Overall, I would not recommend this system and suggest looking at alternatives like the Sony CT-150 for a soundbar. If you really want a 2.1 tower system, there don't seem to be other alternatives in this price range. The closest thing I can think of is the Bose Cinemate II, but that is significantly more expensive.

One last note: I have a Harmony One remote that I setup to use with this system. The system is not very responsive to the Harmony's commands. In order to remediate this, you will need to go through the Harmony application's troubleshooting wizard to change a setting (I think it's called Repeat Rate or something) to 2.

title: It's really a PITA to use
text:
After dealing with DSLR's for video...I saw this camer and was like WOW! Something that would be awesome and easier to use to create HD Videos!!...No so much after I finally got to use it. First off, perhaps the previous owner/user did not charge the battery properly, but it was for sure one of the fastest dying ones out there. I would perhaps get about 1 hour of footage max before the battery died and needed recharging...my other Camera I use for video shoots...swapped out a set of 4x AA's and was still continously shooting.
The user interface is a bother to use, where as on other DSLR's you have dedicated ISO, Exposure, etc, buttons to hit to change the settings...not this sucker...You have only one menu button where you have to navigate the small 3.5" screen to figure where is what. The lowest ISO it goes is 200ASA up to 1600ASA. Where as it would take my 1 sec to change my ISO settings on my other camera...this one required a good 5-10 seconds...going back and forth picking the exact right one.
You can hit the OK button twice to zoom in and better your focus and hit the FOCUS button...but beware of hitting the IRIS button! So many times I wiould have it set to the settings I want, then the camera's shutter angle would dictate otherwise.
Honestly my video from my Fujifilm HS25EXR came out better, especially in lower light settings.
The memory care was another issue...I was finally able to open the .mov files to convert them to .mp4 to edit...since they are HUGE! (40 second shot was 1GB or so)

The audio quality, as obvious to any other DSLR is not even usable, so use a RODE VideoMic or TACSAM recorder to gather your audio

The buk,d quality is NICE, the bottwm door for the battery and SD Card is badly engineered as you are forced to manually push back the pin to keep the door locked.

The screen will desply in green what is in focus, which does help..

In the end after shooting a day with this....I would NOT buy this. I ended up using my HS25EXR (not even a DSLR) for the movie shot since the battery on this dies out way too quickly

Sure it's small and versatile, but it did not suit me...I may just end up getting a Canon T3i and hacking it with black lantern.... for half the price

title: Great sound for a reasonable price
text: I needed more bass and better sound for my Samsung UN46EH5300 led tv. Every since I got my new tv I found the sound to not be as good as my previous lcd samsung tv. Music sounded loud enough most of the time but speech and words was not loud enough. I did a lot of research with sound bars and this one seemed to be the right fit for me. Since I live in a condo, space is limited and I also didnt want something that was too powerful. I do have my 9 year old sony mini shelf system. Its 400 watts, takes up a lot of space and is very outdated. This samsung sound bar has just enough power for me. I use it at 13-15 volume and its plenty loud. The subwoofer is set at 0. I use the cinema setting with 3d cinema. The sound bar is slim enough to fit in front of my tv on the tv stand without coming in the way of the picture or the remote sensor. The subwoofer is also very slim and light. Although the subwoofer is not wireless the wire was long enough for me. I really like that the sound bar has some display indicating the input, volume level, track name for usb and other settings. I am very happy with the sound on this. For tv and movies the audio is crisp and clear with the right amount of bass with overpowering. The sound is also very good for usb and bluetooth. I use my samsung s4 with the bluetooth. The USB port works with flash drives formatted in fat16/32. The user manual said the USB port would play aac audio files, but, I couldnt get it to play any of my itunes aac files that are drm free. I converted the files to mp3 and they played find through the USB port. The sound bar comes with a remote , optical cable and audio cables. I was hoping to use just one remote to control all my devices. But my cable providers dvr remote doesnt work with the sound bar. Overall im very happy with the sound bar, At the price of $150 I find it a very good deal. I was really close to getting the sony htct260 but it was too big and would have come in the way of the screen. Also it was double the price.

title: Full-Featured, Powerful and Affordable Mini-ITX Board
text:
This board was mounted in a Lian Li PC-TU100B aluminum case, along with an Intel Core i5-4690 CPU, Noctua NH-L9I low-profile cooler, EVGA GeForce GTX 750Ti SC Graphics Card, Samsung Electronics 840 Pro Series SSD, Crucial Ballistix Sport DDR3 memory and Silverstone ST45SF-G 450-Watt SFX full modular power supply. Overall, the board and system components have performed flawlessly, scoring a 7.6 on the Windows Experience Index.

The Z97I-PLUS has the latest features geared toward high-performance, including the following:
* LGA 1150 socket (support for Intel 4th gen, new 4th gen and 5th gen processors) / Intel Z97 Express Chipset
* 2 x DIMM (maximum 16 GB) / Dual-channel memory architecture
* 1 x PCI Express 3.0 x 16 slot
* Intel HD graphics support / Graphics ports: DisplayPort / HDMI / DVI-I / D-Sub (VGA) / Support for three displays simultaneously
* RAID 0, 1, 5, 10 and Intel Rapid Storage Technology 13 support / 4 x SATA 6.0 Gb/s ports / 1 x M.2 Socket 3 with M Key
* Intel 1218V Gigabit LAN
* WiFi 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac with dual frequency band 2.4/5.0 Ghz support / External WiFi antenna
* Bluetooth v4.0
* Realtek ALC892 7.1-channel high definition audio / Front panel audio connector / Rear panel optical S/PDIF port
* 6 x USB 3.0 ports (4 ports at rear panel + 2 ports mid-board) / 6 x USB 2.0 ports (4 ports at rear panel + 2 ports mid-board)
* 1 x 4-pin CPU fan connector / 2 x 4-pin chassis fan connectors / Support for both 3-pin (DC) and 4-pin (PWM) fan control modes
* 4 x SATA 6.0 Gb/s cables (2 cables straight connectors / 2 cables 90 degree connectors)
* 1 x WiFi antenna connector

Like other reviewers have mentioned, the WiFi antenna connector is somewhat difficult to install because of its small size. This accessory consists of 2 threaded posts that are installed through the I/O shield and has wires that are just long enough to reach the snap-type pins on the board WiFi controller chip. Perhaps ASUS should have provided some type of board-mounted connector for this feature (similar to that used on MSI Z97 mini-ITX boards), but this is only a minor annoyance and does not detract from the outstanding feature set and overall quality of the board itself.

If you are looking for a fully-featured and reasonably-priced board for your mini-ITX build, this board should definitely be at the top of your list.

title: Someone has to write a realistic review here
text:
Installed this in my 2008 WRX. I thought it'd be fine, I could deal with some stuff not working as long as I could play CD's. I don't need to customize the screen settings, I just want to occasionally listen to music.

Boy, did I get what I paid for.

First of all, this thing is massive. It sticks out a solid 3/4" past the dash. Could just be too big for the car, I'll admit I didn't really try to look before I bought it. Not deducting stars for that.

I had to essentially trim EVERYTHING on the top and bottom of the mounting brackets of my install kit. I went to a couple car audio places looking for one that fit and they both told me they don't exist, I'd have to have one custom made. I gave up and grabbed the dremel after that.

The wiring is ridiculous. Two RCA inputs for audio out for front and rear speakers. Great. But I have two RCA male connections and there's only one RCA input for the sub. Granted if I really thought of this beforehand I could have checked (and I did for the next one I bought) but there's only one picture of this unit, and it's of the front.

None of the buttons underneath the screen light up. Impossible to see at night, which is when I do most of my driving.

You have to tap the screen several times to get it to turn on the touch screen controls, and then there's a delay.

It started playing a CD, then stopped. It does intermittently, but I'm not dealing with it anymore.

Won't connect to bluetooth (two different devices: Note 3 and iPhone)

Won't connect to MP3 player.

The radio works. +1 star.

Because I can't plug in my speaker wires correctly, the sound quality is horrid. Maybe if I rewired my whole system to work with this unit it would sound better, but having high quality speakers everywhere and it sounding worse than my old 89 Mustang isn't cool.

Oh, and when you ARE able to listen to a CD, the screen just shows the terrible looking "TView" logo with a yellow background. Tried to change that and couldn't.

Bottom line is I went cheap and I screwed myself. Maybe if you don't already have a system and you didn't "Accidentally" punch your $1,000 apline head unit, this is right for you. If you actually want something to work and sound good, don't think "Oh this will work fine, blah blah blah I'm just being cheap and stupid" .... just spend the couple hundred bucks more on a double din that both fits, and works.

Pulling it out of the car and sending it back when the new head unit shows up, until then at least it's better than a huge hole in my dash.

title: Could not teach it to respond to remote for new Samsung 55" 4K TV.
text:
I bought this for my mother, who is older and has trouble hearing voices on TV.

The sound quality from this soundbar is very nice. However, I was unable to get it to work with my DirecTV remote control. The DirecTV remote is programmed to control the power/volume for her new 55" Samsung 4K TV (UN55HU6950; Dec. 2014) and works fine. However, the soundbar was unable to properly learn the volume +/- and mute commands from either it, or from the actual TV remote itself. The soundbar was confusing the VOL+ and Mute commands, so every time you try to adjust the volume, you just toggle mute on and off.

I was also unable to train the soundbar to recognize the TV's *original* remote control; perhaps because it's a funky remote that doesn't seem to use plain-old-IR by default.

I'm an engineer and I know technology well, but I found this setup experience maddening. Yamaha needs to work with TV manufacturers on a protocol to send commands over optical (or whatever comes after it), from the TV to the soundbar, to allow the TV to control the soundbar directly (power / mute / volume) so that all of this trouble goes away. The setup is a horrible user experience and even if you get it to work, the solution seems brittle.

My mother is easily confused by technology, so a multiple-remote-control setup is not a good option for her, and I don't want to switch her to a universal remote either (also too confusing). So the soundbar had to go back. We did find that by tweaking the equalizer in the TV's sound settings, we were able to improve the voice clarity to her satisfaction, anyway (by boosting the treble frequencies a bit). I would have loved to keep this soundbar but we just couldn't get it set up properly.

title: Good 3 Meter GPS
text:
I do GPS scouting and soil sampling on ATVs. I was initially interested in the GPS+GLONASS capabilities, 5 Hertz and 10 Hertz Updates, and the claim of improved accuracy. I have tested many of the Garmin 19x HVS capabilities.

POSITIVES
The unit appears solid and waterproof. It is easy to mount. It uses NMEA 0183 (selectable version 2 or 3 using the Garmin utility). I have used it at 38400 and 4800 baud with the included jumper and with multiple computer Applications. I like the 5 Hertz Update rate, the GPS track draws smoother (not sure its more accurate at 5 Hertz, just smoother).

GLONASS
GLONASS was turned off when I received the unit. Using the Garmin utility, I tested GLONASS both on and off. In open fields, GLONASS provides no benefit in my application (I expect the same is true for any GPS application with a clear view of the sky, like a boat). The accuracy with GLONASS turned on was never better than 10 meters (33 feet). The advantage of GPS+GLONASS in this unit is urban (or rural) canyons where only a few satellites in each system are visible. In challenging conditions where it needs both satellite systems to function at all, this unit will do its best.

ACCURACY
With a clear view of the sky, I measured the GPS+WAAS accuracy at better than 3 meters (2D-RMS-95%). With the same view of the sky and GLONASS turned on, the accuracy was worse than 10 meters. The reason for the worse accuracy is that there are no corrections applied to GLONASS satellites (like WAAS is for GPS) when measurements are combined to calculate a fix.

NEGATIVES
The statement "since more overhead satellites are now visible, users will see more accurate fixes in challenging conditions" needs the addition "however in less challenging conditions, your accuracy will be much worse". Where I see less than 50% of the sky, and 10 meter accuracy is acceptable, I would turn on GLONASS.

SUMMARY
Its a good GPS for my scouting applications, and a decent price. I leave GLONASS turned off (as it was configured when I received it). I achieve better than 3 meter accuracy just using GPS+WAAS in my scouting application. I have it mounted with a good view of the sky and the Garmin 19x HVS works fine for my application.

I am also able to shoot video at 1080p HD at 24fps and have had no problems. Others with the 5D have had issues with shooting 1080p video with this Adapter, but that may be because they were using a Class 6 card. I have not had any problems with my Class 10 card noted above.

The only thing I do notice is that if I take a lot of shots (i.e. 5 or 6 shots in the span of 15 seconds), I am not able to immediately play them back, since there is a 10-15 second delay as the photos are written to the card (This is based on shooting 21 Megapixel RAW files).

I was able to save a lot of money using this adapter, since a 64GB SDXC SanDisk card is only about 1/4 the price of a 64GB Compact Flash SanDisk card.

title: My Ammonia Free Windex Cleans Much Better
text: After I've recently bought a macbook pro with retina display, I've decided to buy a cleaning product to keep the macbook clean. Being OCD in every aspect of life especially when it comes to electronics, I've done a vigorous search and research on Amazon, I've come across these products. With all the praise and the hype over the product, I've decided to give it a try. Shipping speed was okay considering I've placed an order along with macbook case & keyboard cover. I bought the whole bundle kit which includes the cloth, iKlear Spray, and more cloths. Turned off my macbook and applied these on the cloth and started rubbing them as explained in the direction. Wiped and wiped but residues were still there and it even looked a little opaque on some of the screen. Left some spots. So I thought I should try the doulbe sided cloth and tried both sides, but I did not see any better result. Thinking hm and hah and just kept rubbing and rubbing it but it just wasn't as clean. And I was like let me try to use Windex, which I've always used to clean my desktop LED monitor. Worked a wonder and removed all the spots this iKlear solution had left & it looked crystal clear. I was just speechless, how my Windex worked better. In Korean proverb, there's a saying that goes "It is better to see it once than hear about it hundred times, and it is better to experience it for yourself once than to see it for hundred times." Reading all these positive reviews somewhat fooled me into thinking that this is the absolute must have product to clean your macbook, but I won't actually know until I try it out myself. Well I learned my lesson and I hope you do too. Please do not be so carried away by all these hyped up reviews.

title: The only bag for a Gitzo traveler size tripod
text:
There are a lot of confusing reviews for this, so I hope I can clear some things up with my recent purchase.

I have the Gitzo 1581OT Ocean Traveler tripod and a Really Right Stuff BH-30 ballhead with lever release.

First I will state that WITHOUT the RRS BH-30 ballhead the Gitzo Ocean Traveler with it's stock stainless steel ballhead will fit snuggly/easily/perfectly in this GC1201T bag.

With the RRS BH-30 ballhead w/ lever release it's a little tricky to fit and zip up. After playing around for about 5 minutes in different ballhead positions, I found one where the bag can fully close without forcing it too much (just a little tug on the zipper). Hopefully I will get around to uploading a picture of it to this gallery.

Would I recommend this bag? Sure, on my other Gitzo 3 series mountaineer, I have the padded Gitzo shoulder strap on it which is more convenient for hiking on trails with (but it's so much more heavier!). Also in how the traveler folds up, I do not think the Gitzo shoulder strap will work well as the legs have to flip/fold out (unless you plan to reattach the shoulder strap each time!), not to mention with it I do not think it will fit in this bag...so it was a trade off with one or the other. I could keep the tripod in it's not folding up position, and instead in the standard closed position and get a bigger bag (like the new Kata adjustable one) with the shoulder strap, but then it just defeats the whole purpose of a compact tripod design IMO.

Yes the shoulder strap on this bag is not padded, but you can always improvise that and make your own out of fabrics, etc. I am about 5'10, and pretty much overweight at 230 pounds and detaching the velcro on the strap end you can extend the strap length like another poster mentioned. The strap does fit around me comfortably (with the exception of no pads on the strap).

The extra pocket on the bag is a welcome to store a bubble level for the hotshoe, snacks, cellphone, and keys or just your standard Gitzo cleaning/repair kit. Most other tripod bags don't even have this outside pocket, so this is a +1 in my book.

I have a logitech revue, like it alot. Would like another gtv for my 2nd tv, using a roku on it for now which would go to the bedroom tv. I'm surprised that Logitech has supported the revue as much as they have but doubt we will see anymore from them or Google. Already seeing must download flash update which of course we cannot do for some sites, so compatibility for future very much in doubt. For those who say pick up a revue instead there's a very good reason not to. Compared to the roku (1st generation) the neo much better but no hulu access. Compared to the revue, like it but the separate IR blaster is awkward, seems to only run one thing at a time and doesn't do that right. My revue can control my tivo and tv, controlling channel changes on tivo, volume thru tv. Neo either can't do it or setup was so hard I gave up. The blaster is powerful enough, I've seen several reviews saying no power, but I can set it up facing away from my entertainment center and it reflects off my white walls and ceiling well enough to control my tv and tivo from the same location. The ir receiver on the tivo and tv are about 3 feet apart.

I use the gtv to watch acorntv and amazon streaming online. On the revue often the first episode of a program will play fine than a shockwave flash crash will mean I need get up and go across the room to pull the plug on revue. No such problem YET with the Neo. If flash crashes a power plug pull needed on revue, power off with power button on remote has worked on neo. Often when using chrome on revue even if I haven't used it for chrome since the last use and not used it for days I will get the tail chasing circle and the page will not load until the power reboot. Haven''t seen that yet on neo.

I like the neo remote. Has all you need in just a handful, not so crowded it's a problem. A little wider grip would be nice but can't have everything. I quickly learned not to wrap my fingers around to the touchpad when using the keyboard so that major dis on the remote is a sign of other reviewers not giving it a fair chance or being somewhat coordination impaired (I'm not known for my coordination to put it in purspective) The touchpad is an awesome concept and usually works well, had to pull batteries once because touchpad wasn't responding but keyboard was. Maybe I was doing something wrong but battery pull did it. Don't know what the control button on the keyboard is for, would have rather seen the shift, control, Fn and caps buttons rearrainged so the most used (Shift and Fn) are on the outside. Also the dedicated HBO to go button? Netgear assumes every one with google tv wants HBO? I would think one of the prime markets would be cord cutters like I am so why the dedicated premium channel button? If you are paying for cable and HBO spring for the sony, not the netgear market IMHO. I would like to see that user defined.

The other media button works great so far on usb source I used. Also access to my picasa account videos. Played them both for hours, no issues.

Crackle great for cheapskates like me. Works great compared to Roku, never bothered with it on Revue.

I wouild NOT recommend this unit at this time to a friend, but a few minor updates and that would change. The one control blaster would have to be fixed, multiple items to control (my case tivo and tv) would have to be fixed. Review has no problems with that.

Would like to see the GTV PrimeTime work. Having cut the cord I don't have cable so chose digital broadcast. Never populated. Tried the local cable company, never populated. No problem with revue so don't think it's me or my location.

Total RAM on revue 520mb. 2gb on neo. Looked all over on the web for specs, found none but response is a little faster than revue and the extra ram explains why it's more stable.

I need this unit to be a little more user friendly so my less tech enthusiastic wife can use it. If the improvements don't come I'll save $80 and get a 2nd roku.

title: Not reall a full disclosure of what the device can and can't do
text: I bought this unit with the understanding that I would be able to control the sound volume of my outdoor speakers that were being fed from my in-house surround sound system in our family room.  When I connected the unit, which is pretty straight forward, there was no sound coming from the outdoor speakers even with the unit volume turned to the highest setting as well as the volume setting on my outdoor speakers.  After corresponding with the manufacturer, I learned that since this NOT an amplifier, the volume on my in-house receiver needed to be at a MINIMUM of 75% full volume for the unit to work.  This was clearly not possible, since we normally listen to the indoor system at about 25% full volume, if we turned it up to 75%, there would be no way to even be in the house, since the volume would be way too high.  I am disappointed in the summary write-up of the device, since it never says that you have to have the volume from the receiver that high to be able to get any sound to any remote speaker, which to me is information that would have been very good to know before I purchased the unit, since if that was known, I wouldn't have bought it.  The manufacturer, however, was very responsive and helped me understand the problem, which was not able to be resolved, so I returned the device.  They did mention that if I could turn off the internal sound, that could work, but that defeats the purpose of having volume control for various speaker systems.  The unit is very well built, seems like a very high quality piece of equipment and I am sure works well, if you can install it in a way that works.

title: Refurbished headset dead in less than 6 months due to known issue
text:
This headset was purchased as a "refurbished" product for about half the regular price on Amazon. Besides not having a box or instructions, there was nothing wrong with them feature-wise.

Headset quality is good overall while it's working. The ear cups will cover your whole ear with quite a bit of room to spare, although if you wear glasses, the pads will begin to disintegrate within just a few months.

The mute button on the side will not always mute the mic - this is a warning to anyone who uses this for work like I do.

Overall the headset is comfortable, although very heavy compared to other similar headsets. But the audio and mic quality is such that it's worth the headache.

The USB port on the Headset finally stopped charging, and this is a known issue with this model. The only way to get it to charge is to sit and hold the two together very firmly at a particular angle to get contact and allow charging to continue. Obviously, this is unacceptable for any sort of work or gaming, and I'm replacing these immediately with the G35 headset, which is similar but wired which will obviously eliminate the issue with the USB charging port going bad.

This headset is good if you have a strong need for wireless with excellent quality. Otherwise, go for the G35 and save yourself the eventual headache of a product that will not function properly in a very short time. It seems that buying new or refurbished won't make much of a difference, so go refurbished and save some cash.

title: Reasonable Projector for simple use
text:
I've got just a few hours of use out of this so far, but enough to get a rough idea. It's a cheap projector, but it works.

There's enough light to see it in a daylight-lit room at a reasonable distance, so it's bright enough. It's reasonably quiet (and has two slightly dimmer modes that run the fan slower). It doesn't get as hot as bulb-based projectors and it starts up and shuts down quickly (no long-running fan at power off).

I've only used it with VGA, but the video quality is acceptable. When feeding it a resolution tuned for the panel's native resolution, it continued to assume roughly 800x600, and just centered the image. I compensated for this by setting a resolution in my video card of 854x480 then letting the video card scale it to 800x600. Imperfect, but.. close enough. HDMI may be more precise, I didn't try it.

There were two things that I felt were worthy of note, because they affect usability. First is that as it warms up, the focus changes, so you will have to adjust the focus frequently until it warms up. This is normal for optics, but higher priced projectors compensate for it.

Second may be a deal-breaker for some. The first time I attempted to use the menu button, it pushed right into the case. I had to dismantle the case to put the plastic back in place - and the mounts used to hold the buttons on are not very good (they looked like plastic rivets that were never melted down to hold it). To me, this was no big deal, but if you aren't comfortable taking apart the case to put the buttons back and lock down the plastic pins (or glue it), then you may want to consider carefully.

Overall, it fit my needs and I will keep it.

title: Nice camera, but not for action photos.
text:
This camera has many great features including multiple settings such as full manual, shutter-priority and aperture priority for those who want to have more control, and the ability to use an external flash (great for indoors when you need more than the on-camera flash can do). The extra-long zoom is also a big plus along with the small easy to handle size and light weight. However, although it says on the Fujifilm website that the HS-20-EXR (no specific mention of this on the HS-30EXR description in fairness) has "Continuous-burst shooting @ 7.6fps (16M) up to 8 frames" on the Fujifilm USA website, my photos on the HS-30EXR were almost all completely blurred and some were just blobs of the players' uniform colors. I thought this FPS feature would be at least as good on the HS30-EXR, but I was unable to capture a lacrosse player running down the field with any clarity. My Nikon D70 did much better at the same event as I was comparing the two side by side.

PS: I just tried adjusting the settings specifically to 8 fps, which is a choice on the sports settings menu, right before submitting this review and still could not get clear pictures of my son running in the yard on a very bright day at ISO 800. In summary, lots of good things on this camera, especially for the price, but shooting action photos didn't work out for me.
