title: Too Many Flaws
text:
I ordered the Fire HD 8.9" 4G LTE version back in September and it arrived yesterday. I had hoped it would be a substantial improvement over the Motorola Xoom but had no real expectations that it would be the so called "iPad Killer." I charged it up with the wall charger and started the registration process. It came preregistered which sort cut the process tremendously. Opted out of the ads (which is don through the website btw NOT the device itself) without a hitch. The problems started when I attempted to activate the AT&T 4G data plan. After filling out the forms on the Fire and submitting them, I still had no 4G after several hours even though the device showed a 4 bar connection. I checked my AT&T iPhone to ensure that there was, in fact, 4G service available -- there was. I did a hard reboot to the device and nada. At that point I went to the manage my kindle website and saw that it shows my account with not one but two Kindles with exactly the same serial number though only one had a kindle email address. Decided to deregister the one with no Kindle email address and they both deregistered. Jumped through the hoops to register it again (not a big deal really) and the same thing happened again. Resubmitted the paperwork for a data plan and waited and waited.

After about 10 hours of nothing (Wifi worked fine btw) I contacted customer service who finally did nothing more than walk me through the various methods of signing up for a data plan -- all of which I had tried -- and claiming they would eliminate the one Kindle too many problem and asking me what I wanted the Kindle named (I choose a different name to see if it actually did change. It didn't and there's still 2 identical Kindles listed) At that point they transferred me to "Kindle People" where I was left on hold for 10 minutes listening to horrid muzak (really). After 10 minutes a voice came on and said rather timidly "Hello?" I answered and explained the problem and she said "I don't know why you're here but you need to call customer service, We don't have anything to do with that." Disconnected at that point. After calling AT&T to see if perhaps they're overwhelmed I was told there's no problem on their end and they couldn't get the device to sign up for a data plan either. They suggested I call Amazon. 24 hours later, still no help from Amazon.

On the bright side, I was able to use the thing with wireless. Pictures look nice. Typing is a chore though, even more so than the Xoom, which is hard to imagine. I'm a careful typist and do expect mistakes, but this thing takes it to all new levels. Then there's the lack of Fire approved app's. One example is the obvious lack of Zinio availability for any Fire (this one or not). The Zinio magazine app is available for every other Android device in the known universe and iPads but not any Fire. And if you've looked at the average magazine subscription on Kindle (or the sheer paucity of magazines compared to Zinio) you'd know why Zinio is preferred. It's lack of availability is nothing more than a method for Amazon to funnel more paying customers into their store rather than Zinio. Offer a superior product for magazines and you won't have to force people into your market. And yes, I'm quite aware there are ways to side load the Zinio app, but that version is now far inferior to the full Android version offered at Amazon's own market.

Packing it up and returning it today for a refund.

title: Underwhelming and Disappointing
text:
I wanted a subwoofer in my car that would "finish" the mostly stock sound system that is lacking in bass. When I purchased the KSC-SW11 I already had low expectations, but I definitely expected that it would produce enough bass to be "good enough". Wrong...and apparently I was expecting too much.

Bass Performance
------------------------------
If you listen to music like rock or anything with acoustic instruments that do not put out demanding bass notes, this may be good enough. The disappointment will come when you try to play any type of music like trance, hip-hop, dance, rap, dubstep, etc - the SW11 just falls flat on its face. It either distorts, or fails to play the notes at all.

Let's be realistic here - nobody expects this little text-book sized subwoofer to shake the car beside you, let alone the seat its under, but it's not unreasonable to expect it to produce audible bass at the frequency levels it claims to be able to.

The bottom line here is that this unit does not sound like a subwoofer; it sounds like a regular mid-range speaker that plays a bit lower than typical. A true subwoofer will have decent volume at least down to 40 Hz...at 40 Hz this thing is praying for you to stop torturing it - it sounds like a dirty old man soiling his drawers.

Build Quality
------------------------------
The unit itself is solidly built. It's in an aluminum case and it's not very heavy - a good and bad thing. The lack of weight indicates that the driver isn't robust (and the sound confirms this), but the aluminum case will ensure that the product is still returnable after you rip it out of your car and throw it off a cliff in frustration.

Adjustability
------------------------------
This unit comes with a wired remote that lets you adjust the volume, cross over and phase. Go ahead and knock yourself out with that, because there is no combination of settings that will make this unit sound remotely good.

Installation
------------------------------
In order to install this 'properly' so you can maximize your disappointment, you will need to run a power wire from the battery to this unit. Included with this unit is a 14 gauge wire, which is good for up to 20 amps of current. When your car is running you have 14 volts on your circuit, which means that you can draw 280 watts of power, max (volts x amps = watts). The wire for the amp is fused for 15 amps, so using the included wire is more than adequate to power the puny 75 Watt RMS amplifier in this subwoofer.

After you run the power cable you will need to connect your head unit to the audio inputs of the subwoofer, either by using the RCA-type line level connectors or by splicing into your speaker level wires (if your head unit does not have RCA outputs).

Finally, you will need to ground the unit by connecting the ground lead to an unpainted metal part on your car's body. You can shorten this if you want.

Once it's all hooked up, you can adjust the crossover, volume and phase. A good starting point is to set the the high-pass filter for your main speakers to 80 Hz and the subwoofer's low-pass filter to 100 Hz...well, that's a good starting point if you have a subwoofer that actually produces bass below 80 Hz. This one distorts quite heavily once it gets down to about 60 Hz and by the time it's at 40 Hz you can't even hear it.

Appearance
------------------------------
Not that it matters because this thing is stashed under a seat, but it does look nice.

Conclusion
------------------------------
I cannot rate this product highly because it does not perform as well as it should. The spec of this subwoofer claim it can play sound frequencies between 35 Hz to 125 Hz - it's basically inaudible below 60 Hz and when the bass line of a song is demanding the amplifier shows how it is unable to keep up. You will find that the bass you get with a good set of main speakers do better than this unit.

For what it's worth, the enclosure for this unit is very small, it's sealed and not ported, plus the driver is mild. From a physics standpoint, the ability of a speaker to achieve a certain level of volume depends on its ability to move air - there are such things as low-powered subwoofers that actually sound decent. I have several and this is not one of them.

I haven't had time to uninstall this yet but when I do, I plan to return it and build my own subwoofer from scratch.

title: Im appauled by the negative reviews
text:
Where am I coming from in this review? From having owned a pair of Sennheiser 518s, Senheiser 280 pros, and Beryodynamic 250s. These are hands down some of best sounding headphones I have heard. In my opinion it has the best balance of all things.

You have to divide a headphone by two principle catagories:

1. The quality of the drivers
2. The EQ.

The reason I say this is many headphones out there have their own unique EQ. Some are more treble oriented, others mid bassy, etc. These tend to be in my opion a great balance of everything. They definatly DO NOT lack mids or bass. The treble can carry a bit of sssymbalice depending on your source. On my pc with an external 24 bit sound blaster live card, this becomes apparent, but creative already puts an emphasis on these frequenies as it is. On my LG Optimus G pro, its a differnt story. I hook these up to it and wam. Im right there in a studio.

Comfort: There extremely comfortable. It feels like two memory form pillows sitting around both ears.

People are complaining about a buzzing. I hear no buzzing. You can NOT call the noise cancelation being turned on as creating a loud buzzing. You can tell power is turned on but its not even close to loud. Its an electric circuit thats making that possible. Once I start playing anything at all at normal regular listening volumes its perfectly fine. Know what your buying people! These are noise cancleing headphones that require battery power to be turned on. There will be a minor sound on all sets like this, even bose.

Frequency: These can rattle your brain when called upon, but not regularly like people are saying. It doesnt take something thats not there and say well how about some more bass here and lets muddy this! No these are very very very clear and open. Ill say that again: They are VERY CLEAR AND OPEN sounding. They are in my opinion very neutral. Unlike a lot of headphones out in the market there not a V. They dont just have bass and treble. The mids shine on these cans. Which leads me to my next point.

Driver quality: When push comes to shove You can adjust eqs all day. You can take the sennheiser 280s for instance and give them more bass, and treble, but there will be a limit to how good you can get them depending their drivers. I have put these headphones on about 7 people with a good jazz piece. Every person I put these cans on said they were the best pair of headphones they had heard. They didnt say oh well theres a humming noise or anything of the sort (because the music was playing which is a normal phenomenon for people who are wearing headphones). This was with the EQ flat. I personally think that if ONE thing needs to be adjusted Eq wise, its the treble. The 16hz needs a few cranks down...but again a lot of it depends on your source! Im listening on my PC right now and have some things adjusted in spotify to make these headphones sound exactly like they do hooked up to my cell phone without any EQ. But the point of brining EQ into focus again is to make the point that I can adjust the EQ and because they have rich full sounding drivers in them, it wont matter if I do. I will also ad that I put my sennheier 280s (which have over 1000 4.5 reviews) and compared these two sets. This pulverizes them. Theres hands down no competition.

In conclude by stating this. I bought these used a trading store. I saw them under 200, tried them on and was sold within about 5 minutes of listening to various tracks. I was 100% positive going out of that store that when I got home and read these reviews they would be rave about these cans. I like to buy good products and im into sound (kappa 8s, polk monitor 70s, etc) Instead I come on and see all the negative stars. I shouldnt even have to be mentioning them, they just shouldnt be there. Having used them for over a week now, I felt guilty not contributing to the five star club on these cans. They are 100% worth the 170 dollars I paid for them. Just make sure your driving them with the right source. A lot of this depends on source! Headphone amps can be benificial for some sets, and these could use them slightly on phones (depending on the phone)...but on my LG Optimus phone (no special DAC in that) they sound phenominal with Jazz and every well recorded song Ive put at them. Im not a beats or bose can by nautre. ANd I cant stand headphones that have muddy or overpowering base. I like CLEAN SOUND. These have them clearly in the mids, have good solid bass, but wont rattle your head so hard you loose brain cells.

title: Excellent value for what it is
text:
If you are looking to buy this item, it's important to consider what the purpose of such a laptop/netbook device is. It's not the most powerful option for high end processing, but for basic computing, I really feel there's no better value for the money.

Positives:

Price/performance ratio is high. Much higher than an Atom based netbook.

Easy to open and upgrade. No screws to open.

One 4GB DIMM with one open slot, supporting up to 8GB.

Smaller form factor. It feels like a 10.1 netbook in size, but nicer screen size than 10.1 netbooks. I actually had to return the 11.6 case I bought for it and buy a case for a 10.1 size. It fit!
Keys are nicely spaced and really full-size.

Runs quite cool and quiet after removing the unnecessary features of the HP software components.

Drivers are easy to locate online, unlike many, and they actually work when installed. Some manufacturers make driver location difficult, and they never work quite right, in my experience. Not the case here. I swapped for an SSD, which I'd recommend, and replaced drivers easily and every component and function works perfectly.

You only need to download 7 drivers in total to restore all hardware functions (Ethernet, Wifi, Trackpad, Catalyst, IDT audio, on screen display, and bluetooth.)

Amazon customer service is great.

Negatives:

This model is NOT the imprint finish, despite what the details say in the info, or at least the one I purchased in March wasn't. As such, it shows fingerprints a bit, but nothing terrible.

The Synaptics trackpad is improved with physical buttons, but still buggy as all heck. Don't expect Mac-like smooth functioning here. The two-finger scroll feature rarely works correctly. All others are fine. I use it with and without a mouse, and it's fine, but one must adapt to it.

Keys are a bit plastic feeling. I'd have preferred a rubberized finish to them, as they are quieted by the finish also. The plastic keys are a bit clacky when typing.

text:
Decent television if you can get a good deal on it (I paid $357.00 with shipping and taxes included in this price), but two somewhat annoying drawbacks. Think of it like this; draw a shape - square, circle, triangle, or whatever - with solid, straight, sharp lines. Then draw the same shape with a shaky hand and the pencil barely touching the paper. And the worst part is, there is nothing in the settings that can fix this; I tried adjusting them for two days. Now, again, this is only noticeable on certain images and usually only when there is slow movement.

The other problem was that it does not come with any screws for the base, and you only find that out if you read the manual cover-to-cover and are lucky to notice the small sentence in there regarding this ridiculous oversight. I mean, how cheap and miserly is Sharp to not include an obviously necessary, yet very small and inexpensive part??? I had to search seven different hardware stores to find screws that were the proper length and width, and had the correct type of threading on them.

Other that those two things it's an ok tv set. The sound is slightly above average, considering the size of the speakers, and other than the occasional issue that I've mentioned, the picture is pretty nice.

title: CAUTION: Filter are BLACK for a reason...forget the SILVER ones...forget the BLACK too, not multicoated
text:
This filter comes in either black or silver, which are fine for the exterior rim, but not for the interior rim. When a filter is attached to the lens, it extends the barrel a bit. No lens barrel is ever painted silver because no one want stray light reflected into the lens. Whoever designed/made the filter probably does not know this simple principle. I ordered the silver to match the look of the my silver lens, never thought about the interior rim color until I screwed it on. It's an immediate return. Amazon should not sell these in silver and, if they do, at least put up a big warning in ALL CAP.

Added 12/22/2014: Putting the rim color aside, I should note that the 46mm glass I got was not multicoated upon quick inspection. Coatings are applied on glass to improve transmission. The effectiveness changes with wavelength (color). So the coating would weaken the reflection intensity of a yellowish light bulb and make it look greenish. That's what happened with a 37 mm Fatasy glass I bought from a "sold by Amazon" listing. The 46mm glass from this listing shows bright yellow reflection. So brand name does not mean anything. There is no quality control.

title: Sleek, quiet, and fast.  The perfect combination.
text:
Overall I am exceptionally pleased with this hard drive because it is very fast, small and quiet for a 500 GB drive. It uses USB 3.0 which provides users a huge data transfer speed advantage over previous technology (USB 1.0 and 2.0). Obtaining this device actually forced me to upgrade my computer to accept USB 3.0 connections, which was very easy to do. For the sake of anybody who is interested in fast data transfer speeds and doesn't have USB 3.0, I'll spend a minute describing what I did to upgrade my computer's hardware.

I had not paid much attention to USB technology advancements over the years because my computer is four years old and uses USB 1.0. Frankly I wasn't sure what USB 2 or 3 was until I did a little research. Using USB 3.0 is awesome because the data transfer speeds are 20-30 megs per second, which is WAY faster than what I am used to with USB 1.0. Here is the bottom line - if you plan to move a lot of pictures, music files, or documents back and forth between your computer and this external hard drive, then you need to upgrade your USB port to 3.0. Trust me, it is worth it. Upgrading is very easy. Just order the USB 3.0 board (around $30) and install it in your computer. I purchased a 3.0 board from Amazon, "Western Digital SuperSpeed USB 3.0 PCI Express (PCIe) Card", and it took 15 minutes to install. Final note on USB 3.0 - you don't need it to use this hard drive, so don't worry about it if faster speeds are not a purchasing requirement for you.

The hard drive works like any other external memory device. Connect the device to your computer and it behaves like an internal hard drive. I use GoodSync synchronization software to manage data between my computer and external hard drives. You can skip the fancy software and simply copy/paste if you like, or you can invest $30-50 for file transfer software which I'd highly recommend for advanced users.

In summary, I'd recommend this product because it works great and it is very tiny and fast. The sleek metal casing is good looking and appears very durable.

title: solid product
text:
I like this tripod a lot, it is very stable compared with the cheap beginner's tripod I used before. Suddenly, my pictures became sharper and looked better.

It is maybe a bit on the heavy side but, since I mainly use it for landscapes, it stays in car and the effort to bring it on location is acceptable.
The pistol head brings a lot of flexibility and easiness in composing the shots. The price for the flexibility is again some additional weight.
With so many configuration options the flexibility of this system truly deserves 5 stars.
But, If I would have to buy another tripod I would bite the bullet and go for the lighter carbon version and a lighter ball-head (provided the combo would still support the same weight)

I only gave it 4 stars because, it is important to mention a problem I had during my vacation in CA where I used the tripod for seascape pictures.
The ocean waves were pretty strong and the tripod legs got clogged by the sand that crept in.
I tried to clean it each time, but you can only take care of the external parts. The legs got scratched since I couldn't move around without pushing them back in.

After reaching home, it took me half a day to dismantle the entire system to the very last nut and bolt and clean the inner parts.
The surgery was successful and the tripod works very smoothly again.

Next time I'll be away for more than 1 day, I'll have some tools ready to perform the job on the spot, if needed. And I'll be a little more careful, of course.
However, I believe most of the tripods out-here would have had the same faith when battered by those strong waves.

Update: I went for another ocean photography trip and, this time, I made sure the lower sections were always (at least partially) extended. I pushed them back in only after washing them in fresh water. The tripod returned home without any problems.

I recommend the purchase as one of the best value for money options.

3 month update: I'm still liking this tablet a lot and has a good mix of productivity and entertainment capability. I was briefly swayed by the new Google Nexus 7 but this tablet has been a great fit. The s-pen is indispensible for working with pdfs and when using the note taking software. It does a great job of capturing my handwriting quickly and accurately. The included Polaris Office allows one to manage office files on the go and to review presentations without having to buy additional software. I have used it on multiple flights and the video playback is very nice.

Bottom line: This is a great business and entertainment tablet that is a quantum leap from my iPad 1. If you don't need to work with highlighting/note taking then the s-pen may not hold a lot of value for you and you may be served better by Samsung's other s-pen-less tablets. If your priorities are gaming/HD video/the crispest screen then look at the Nexus or retina iPads. If you want a well-balanced tablet that's reasonably priced and offers the expanded capability of the s-pen then look no further.

text:

I own a Nest, largely because it looks beautiful in my home, but I also found that it was not only a wealth of knowledge but it saved me a bunch of money as well (and saving money means more automation!). This is why I ultimately bought myself a SkyDrop as well. I did my due diligence looked at some of the other "Smart Sprinkling" systems, and even KickStarted one. In the end, none of them were that marriage of esthetics as well as knowledge and technology that SkyDrop is.

SkyDrop comes beautifully packaged and I was able to swap out my old Hunter unit in about an hour. Once that was done, there is a very simple process on the SkyDrop to connect it to your home network. At this point I was able to connect to it from both my phone and the SkyDrop website. The amount of customization is amazing and brings a whole new world to sprinkling your lawn.

Now some people may scoff at a smart sprinkling system, but there were no longer areas of my lawn with mushrooms, or dried out areas, my lawn as a whole looked green and healthy (I think a lot of us just kind of give up on our lawns at some point). The data nerd in me was then able to go back in my phone, and see what days the controller had watered my lawn as well as see the moisture my lawn got from the fall rain storms.

This all leads back to what I love about the automation I chose. I saw almost immediate savings on my water bill. I was no longer watering my lawn no matter what. This device was paying for itself right away.

title: V5-171-9661: apparently SATA2 only speed + Computrace LoJack activated.
text:
My V5-171-9661 would have been a great laptop, had it not suffered from the two following major issues:

1) It delivers only SATA2 (3Gb/s max) speed with Samsung 840 Pro 256GB SSD (~250MB/s reads). The laptop has the latest BIOS v2.15 in AHCI mode and the latest Intel Rapid Storage drivers. Both Intel RST tool and Samsung SSD Magician tool report SATA2, while the laptop's HM77 chipset is known to be SATA3-capable (6Gb/s). The same Samsung SSD used to deliver ~520MB/s with my old Lenovo SATA3-capable system. Now I'm not sure if it's only this specific machine, or the whole line of V5-171-9661 is affected. I'd appreciate if someone with the same model + SATA3 SSD could post his/her results.

2) The laptop came with Absolute Software Computrace/LoJack feature pre-activated. The BIOS doesn't have any settings to turn it off or even see check its status at all. It survives the hard drive swap, complete OS reinstall and keeps creating a set of executable files (rpcnet*.exe, rpcnet*.dll) in system folders. Basically, it is a kind of controversial BIOS rootkit, which seamlessly reports your laptop location (along with other demographics) to Absolute's servers. I have no plans to subscribe to Absolute's services and I don't want my laptop to call any 3rd party without my explicit consent. So far I've been unable to find a way to disable or kill Computrace. I contacted both Acer and Absolute and I am still waiting to hear from them. However, from what I googled on that matter, the chances to get rid of this "feature" appear to be less than zero. Again, my old Lenovo also had this feature in BIOS, but it arrived in inactive state, and I was able to disable it permanently in BIOS.

Two stars taken off.

title: They've baited everyone with cosmetics. Now we're screwed.
text:
I was so impressed with the thought of what this product was supposed to do, that I looked beyond the multiple negative reviews. Obviously there are people that have odd occurances, but this product is full of so many issues with things that are standard and advertised, it's truly disappointing. You're welcome to you own opinion, but what I will do is site very specific things that owners have been begging Motorola to make right for over a year, and there is still no resolve.

1.) They boast that you can plan and create a route, transfer it to the watch, and navigate through a workout. There's an entire Planning area on the portal for this. However, when you manually create a route, like you're able to in GarminConnect, MapMyRun, and many other sites, the line does not follow the roads as it does when you create it. When it transfers to the watch it only connects the points that you place; does not follow roads. Why not click points at every turn you ask...because you're only allowed up to 20+ before you exceed the limit. Now, with an entire area devoted to this, and the supposed possibility that you can share with other users, you would think that this would be a primary fix. Yet, I have left multiple thread requests, as well as many other people in the forum, only to have the same issues since the first thread in November, 2011. So, basically the image they show on the advertisement of navigating a planned route is not true; makes the Planning are completely useless. While navigating on a bike you cannot follow the route, so you are forced to stop and fugure it out. If auto pause is on, the device pauses and there is no access to the map.

2.) Portal Bugs - Incorrect elevation, elevation does not show up on chart on MANY occasions, competitions do not accrue mileage on timeframes specified, interval training and the design of custom workouts has always had issues and still does after many attempts to fix. I can go on and on but I'll just ask that you go to the forum and see the complaints for yourself. These are only a few. See the rest at [...]
3.) Testing of the device was very poor prior to being released in November 2011; it should never have been released, but Motorola seems to have taken the position that they do with cell phones and assumed that everyone will replace these devices every 1-2 years (Motorola Q - junk). Testing is also very poor when updates and fixes are provided. They attempt to fix or add something and it is rarely brought to the finish line. Also, when attempts to fix are made, there are certain to be indirect problems that arise. Again there are complaints about so many areas of this device it's amazing there isn't a class action suit. I expect to see one in the near future and I will join along with the thousands of others that have unresolved issues.

4.) Music/MP3 - constantly stops and starts during a workout. They say to deactivate the headset control as a solution. So, I bought a device and need to deactivate a control so it will actually work. In addition, that did not work for many users, and they still have no resolve.

5.) Website - Constantly down or very slow. Syncing workouts becomes a major pain. There are constantly errors when accessing the site, sometimes for weeks at a time, when getting in is rare; errors are plenty.

6.) Customer Service - Oh it's great when you first buy the watch, or have something positive to say. Look at the forum and tell me how many times you see "we're sorry. we'll look into the problem". They need to realize that this shouldn't be acceptable. Bottom line, the device shouldn't have been released.

If you're willing to be part of a beta test, then buy this. Be prepared; the honeymoon phase lasts for a little while until you realize all of the problems there are. The six things I have listed are only an ant's fart in a hurricane. I couldn't possibly state them all.

I am going back to Garmin. Motorola could have run the market, but I know too many people that have returned this device, and too many people that are frustrated with it. They have damaged what could have been a great reputation. Motorola is more concerned with the casual workout crowd for two reasons. First, they love the cosmetics and calorie counters,and album cover that displays when the MP3 player actually works. Second, they don't try to use the devise for the purposes it advertises, and the features that make athletes want to track and increase their progress. Endurance athletes, marathon runners, cyclists, and trail runners should all stay away from this device. In addition, those of you that do want music, phone, and heart rate capabilities, the battery life with those things being used is 4-hours if you're lucky.

Again, you don't have to believe me. Please go to the MotoACTV forum and see all of the complaints.

title: Solid product with room for improvement
text:
The connection seems as reliable as other bluetooth products I've used (which all tend to stutter/buffer/cut out for a second in my experience). If you're an audiophile or aren't bothered by wires, you're probably not looking at these anyway. I love the compact, simple design. They easily drape around your neck when you're not wearing them. Although they come with 3 sizes of ear buds, none fit my ears well. The larges fit the best, but didn't seal well at all. I replaced them with the foam isolation buds, and it made a world of difference! The proper seal increased the sound quality of these headphones substantially. If you have any doubt on if the seal of the stock buds are adequate, replace them with the foam buds.

Next, I use the headphones with my Android, and I have yet to find an app that can control the buttons. There are plenty of apps that do this for wired headsets, but apparently similar apps for bluetooth headsets are harder to come by. There is no way to program the buttons out of the box either. The standard play/pause, previous, and next actions are fine, but I hate that holding down the center button redials. When I think I'm bringing up Google Now, it redials, then I have to frantically pull out my phone to end the call.

Also, when certain button actions are initiated, there is a voice that says things like "power on" or "redial". That's fine, but again, there is no way to control it. I would like to be able to reduce the volume or turn it off all together.

I've just harped on the negatives, because most of the positives are already outlined in other reviews. These are a great product, they quality sound (with foam tips!), long battery life, and connect with very little issues. My biggest complaint is lack of button control (which may be solvable with an app).

title: Everything not great, more problems...
text:
This is my first HDTV purchase. I waited a long time for them to come down in price, and am very happy with this TV so far. I've had it for about 3 weeks now and it is working great. I've watched various movies, the Euro Cup games, MLB All-star game, etc. As many have pointed out, it has a great picture, but may need some tweeking to get it how you want. This isn't hard to do if you have basic technology skills (i.e. finding the "Menu" button on remote and going to "Picture," then playing around with settings). Again, as others have noted, sound is okay. I'm not an audiophile or anything, but like good audio. I'll probably get a sound bar at some point, but it's just fine for now. I would not let others criticism of the sound deter you from buying this TV. I have not used the internet ready features, but will once I get a wifi blue ray player hooked up so can't comment there.

The biggest issue with the TV is what others have noted - Panasonic's shoddy packaging. This really surprises me considering the quality of TV. Spend a few more pennies to get an extra layer of card board in there! My box had several holes punched right through it (thanks Fed Ex), fortunately they were all in the back which had more room for error (extra inch or two of depth) than if it were in front where the screen was. If the holes were in the front, whatever punched through the box probably would've damaged the screen.

To summarize - excellent TV that I'm very happy about. Great price, especially with no tax and free shipping. I got the TV, the Mediabridge HDMI cable, and a 3 year warranty for less than what I would have paid for just the TV at a local big box store before tax! Not sure how Amazon does it, but I'm happy to benefit from their methods. The only thing here is you are rolling the dice having such a large item shipped. Be home when it arrives, inspect the box, give it a whirl. If it doesn't work or has damage then send it back. From the feedback I've read, Amazaon is very good about this. Fortunately I did not have to deal with it. I did take pictures of the damaged box though as a precaution.

I'll update this in the future if anything changes, but otherwise am very happy! Wait for it to go on sale and Prime it!

8/2/12 UPDATE - I've begun to notice vertical banding - vertical, translucent lines that almost look like shadows, and range in width from 1" to 4" across the entire screen. This is PARTICULARLY noticeable when I have been watching olympic soccer or baseball games with the green background when the camera is panning or following the action quickly. You see it at other times when there is a bright background and the camera is moving. I've also noted when objects move quickly in movies or shows there is some serious distortion. Other 95% of time picture is great. It is not an HDMI cable or input issue. This is a 120hz TV, so it should not be a refresh rate issue IMO. Here are some links on the topic as it appears to be a common problem w/ LCD and LED tv's.

[...]

8/7/12 UPDATE - I see they wouldn't allow me to include my links from my last update...oh well. So the technician came to my house today and noticed the problem right away. I guess that does make it a "serviceable issue." We enjoyed watching some of the Brazil and S. Korea match for a while. He tried a few things. We reproduced it on other channels and on a DVD. He said it's not the panel or backlight as he put it to a blue screen and everything was perfect. His best guess was something is wrong with the refresh rate for whatever reason, and noted that since it is a 120hz TV it should not be happening. He said he has not seen this particular issue before, and it looked comparable to what most 60hz TV's look like. He called it in and described it as a "noisy background." The person on the other end of the phone tended to agree so they are replacing the "main board" on the TV. On the receipt it is noted as a "Main PCB," and is a $262 repair. The part is being delivered to my house and repair scheduled for next week. I'll continue to update as it happens.

8/16/12 UPDATE - Same tech came back today and replaced the main board. This did not solve the problem. He tried adjusting settings, called into his office to talk to technician who is particularly knowledgeable about settings and calibration, still no luck. He did say that issues like this are not uncommon in LCD/LED TV's. Next step is to call Panasonic and see what they say. Problems seems undetectable to some, others notice it immediately.

9/23/12 UPDATE - Wow. Where do I begin. I'll start out with this - Panasonic's customer service is an epic nightmare. That's a pretty good summary. I'm now a month and a half into dealing with them. I've made 5-6 calls to them since my last post in August, spent hours in discussion with them, hours on hold, hours being disconnected, hours being re-routed to the wrong people and the wrong department. In a word, incompetent would be putting it nicely. The service company who came out to service the TV declared it non-repairable back in August. Panasonic claimed they never did this. And around and around we go. There are so many stories I don't even know where to begin. On one call I was told that I could not speak to a supervisor and that I could not leave a message for one. End of phone call. Seriously. It's just insane. This past Friday I spent over an hour with them on the phone as they told me my "TV was working to specifications and would not be replaced." It really took them over a month to determine this? When I asked for a full clarifcation as to why, again, they are cherry picking information from the repair company. I was told I would need to call the repair company as they would not replace the TV unless the repair company changed their report. I called them (A&E Repair) and they were responsive, friendly, and competent. What a change. We now have an appointment for the same tech to come to my home on Wed. to verify the problem is still occurring (which it is). Then we are going to call Panasonic together and tell them the TV needs to be replaced. A&E said this way Panasonic cannot claim that the TV was never called in as unrepairable, again.

At this point Panasonic is at least guilty of incompetence in their customer service and warranty department. At worst, they are disingenuous, lying, and not standing by their product in an attempt to get me to give up my attempts at getting a working product. What they have yet to learn is that I'm pretty persistent and they've chosen the wrong customer to do this to. I've yet to decide if I will report them to the Better Business Bureau yet. Since my TV is "working to specs" and the problems people have actually acknowledged exist are "normal," nothing is going to happen. My last ditch effort is an email to the Panasonic technician dept. he was speaking to, along with attached photos and videos of the problem. As always, I'll post their response.

This review has become a book and is silly by now, but for me it's the principle of the matter at this point. I'm glad to see the time I've taken to write this has actually deterred people from buying this product. Hopefully more of you continue to comment.

10/31/12:
Happy Halloween. No trick here, I'm actually getting my TV replaced. So I was able to take video and photo proof of the problems on the TV. I emailed it to Panasonic at the address they requested and surprise, surprise, no response after 2 weeks. I then filed a Better Business Bureau case and had a call from the North American branch of Panasonic within 48 hours. The employee that called me was friendly, professional, and re-assured me right out of the gate that my TV will either be replaced or my money back - my choice. I was informed however, that my current one could not be repaired. I asked them how that could be when they were willing to replace it, but yet other staff had told me it was "working to specs." This is no lie now - I was actually asked if I was recording the conversation. I reassured them I was not. I was then told that it is known internally that there are problems with Panasonic LED line of televisions. REDEMPTION!

The employee said that they could not repair the issue because techinically it was within their accepted specs, and that they could not comfortably replace it with the same model as it would be likely that the replacement would have the same issues. In talking to a friend who works at out local Best Buy, he told me that they had not received any Panasonic LED shipments in a while and his guess was maybe they are actually doing something about this now.

Anyway, I was offered a full refund, or an upgrade to a Panasonic plasma TV that was much nicer, larger, and a lot more features. I took the TV and I talked them into giving me the next model up from what they offered me an even exchange for due to my troubles. Basically I'm getting a $1200 TV for my orginal price of $750. My Square Trade Warranty also transfers over. I have the employee's direct line so I will be dealing only with them for any future issues - another reason I was willing to take another Panasonic. I'm waiting for the TV to be delivered to a local business who will be delivering it to my door and taking away the "old" one. Hopefully I'll only be writing one more review after this professing love for my new TV. If you are having the same problems that I had, save yourself a lot of stress and wasted time and just open up the BBB case if Panasonic is dragging their feet.

I win...maybe

11/30/2012:
I've had the replacement for almost 2 weeks now (got delayed due to demand and Hurricane Sandy...seems right for my luck in all this). I talked them into giving me a TC-P50ST50 plasma unit as an even exchance. A regional repair company sent a technician out to pick up the old one and set-up the new one. The replacement TV they gave me is absolutely stellar. The plasma picture is far superior to the LED I had. The sound is also much better. It truly is a pretty spectacular TV. Unfortunately, the stock Netflix app is not working on it. Fortunately I do not have to go through Panasonic anymore. The repair technician from the delivery company is in direct contact with their tech dept and is handing it. Panasonic tried to say it was b/c I have too low bandwith - something I thought was plausible considering I only get 3mbps to my house. So I had my cable company bump me up to 15mbps (plenty of bandwith for the app) for a day to see what would happen. I verified via a speed test that I was up and running at 15mbps. It did not solve the problem. I think the app was corrupted on install or something. The technician is awaiting a response from Panasonic at this time. The fun continues...

1/10/2013:
The Netflix issue was resolved without repair, but rather by some help from the Amazon community. It actual was likely happening due to Comcast intentionally restricting bandwith to the TV (apparently something they readily admit they do to other on-demand competitors). Once I changed the IP address on the TV to the public Google server, the app has worked just fine since then. The replacement plasma TV I received is fantastic. I'm very happy with it.

title: Hope Springs Eternal . . .
text:
It took 3 Paperwhite IIs to get at least a 4-star Paperwhite II reader, but I just couldn't resist the advertised improvements of the Voyage. My husband had inherited my Paperwhite I. My first Kindle was the Touch. Even after reading reviews before the Voyage arrived a week ago, hope springs eternal. I bit the bullet and went all out for $289 thinking the odds were pretty good for me to receive one of the few good units being shipped.

Overall, I love the idea, improvements and intent of the Voyage, but for $289 I really expected a good, even-lighted screen. Mine is not; same story here -- yellow at the top. Compared to my Paperwhite II, however, the screen lighting is actually better. But, for the cost "better" is not enough; it should be perfect.

The tactile page-turn buttons are just "OK." When the pressure is turned down to make it easier for these old arthritic hands, I find that just picking up the Voyage often turns pages and I have to find where I left off. The buttons would have been more convenient if they were a little higher toward the top of the reader, so I have to adjust where I naturally hold it. With the narrower edges, however, the touchscreen works even better than the Paperwhite.

The auto-bright feature works well for me, and I really like the flat screen. Again, with narrower edges and flat screen the touchscreen is easier to use.

I hate the origami cover. My first one was the plastic one from Belkin which was a real piece of junk. This $60 leather Amazon cover feels nice, but I prefer a standard "book-opening-type" cover. This one is more clumsy to open and I would never use the stand-up feature it offers.

As much as I hate to, I'm returning the Voyage. I will definitely order again later when the screen lighting irregularities are corrected. I don't know if just a software update will fix the lighting problem. Do I have to just wait for Voyage II?

title: DON'T BUY ACER
text:
I wish I could give ZERO star to Acer. I bought this PC in March 2011. After a few months, I had to send the computer to Acer four times for repairs. The problem has always been the same: system freezes on startup, and often while using the computer.... usually on the 2nd or 3rd day after completing various Microsoft Updates.

First they replaced the harddrive. The computer continued to freeze at every start up. The second time, they replaced the memory. This time the computer worked for 1 day. The third time, they changed the upper plastic case and it only worked two days. So I had to call the customer service the fourth time. This time I talked with level 2. The level 2 guy was very nice. He promised me that technician will diagnosis the problem and they will make sure to send me back a normal computer.

However, that is not the end of story. After two weeks, the PC was back. This time they changed mother board. Today was my first day use, the system did not freeze. Good Job, Acer! But the explorer kept telling me the certificate was expired whenever I tried to login facebook, hotmail, or gmail. After three restarts, the problem finally fixed by itself. In the meanwhile, the window update is not working, even though I tried to do it manually. So I had to call Acer the fifth time. The customer service manager said that I had to talk with level 2, since my PC had sent back more than 3 times. And I had to call back tomorrow, since level 2 is closed on Sunday. Okay, I will keep testing the computer, and see if the freeze problem is still here. If anyone know how to get the update works, welcome to send your comments.

To save your trouble, don't buy Acer!

title: I love my Nighthawk routers!
text:
I already purchased Netgear's model previous to this one (NETGEAR Nighthawk AC1900 Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7000)) and have been using it for 9 months now and have loved it. Naturally when I got the opportunity to try out the next revision in the Nighthawk series, I had to jump on it.

I haven't had this router long enough to vouch for its reliability, but I would like to say that I have only had to reboot my other Nighthawk once in 9 months I had it, and I'm not sure I really had to do it then, either--I decided later that it was more likely my guest's wireless device that was the culprit.

If you haven't yet had the privilege of using 802.11ac, you're missing out. 802.11n is fine, I suppose, but after using ac, the difference is painfully obvious and I use the ac band whenever possible. There is a major caveat, though--not all devices support ac. Many of the Apple devices I've tried didn't support it, my Chromecast doesn't support it (alas--it could really have used it, too) and of course anything more than a few years old won't support it, either. Another important caveat is that the 5GHz band does not travel as far and through as many walls as the 2.4GHz band does. This router does both so if you are out of range on the 5GHz band, you can set your devices to automatically switch to the 2.4GHz band.

Speaking of range, both of my Nighthawk routers KILL my previous DLink 802.11n router's range. I keep my router in the basement and the old router's signal was lost as soon as I went outside. My Nighthawk routers allow me to roam through most of my yard before losing the signal (granted, it's a fairly small yard at < .25 acre). Note that I have not observed any significant difference in range between the 2 Nighthawks.

Set up
I've never been one to use set-up wizards on my routers. I can understand that some people may really appreciate them and that those same people probably need it to come up as the default choice, but personally, I just skip them and configure the router manually. I have encountered routers in the past that strongly discourage you from doing that by making it difficult to get to the manual configuration section--I've even had some prevent direct access completely until after you agree to their privacy policy, set up an account on their web site, etc. (WHAT?! exactly!). I'm pleased to say I didn't have to do any of that here. By the same token, I appreciate that the router comes preconfigured with a unique SSID and WPA password (or at least, I assume they are unique) and that those bits of data or on an easily removable sticker on the router itself. I think that is the most perfect way of having security out of the box without being obtrusive or annoying.

The web page you go to to manage it is quick and easy to use. It has all the features you would expect in a SOHO router and then some including port forwarding/triggering, usage metering, VPN service (I have not tested this yet), static route management, guest networks (2), wireless AP mode, parental controls, scheduling, etc.

I will point out that routers seem to be getting bigger and bigger these days and this one is one of the largest I've ever used. That isn't necessarily a big deal and it is understandable since it is operating 3 wireless bands instead of just 1 and beam-forming requires at least 2 antennas to work and those antennas need to be spaced apart. However, if your old router fit pretty snugly into a certain spot, make sure you leave enough space for this one. Note also that with the faster processor and stuff inside, this router may need more breathing room than your old one did. It's totally worth it, though--make the space and upgrade.

For those who care, my Kill-A-Watt says that under a light load, this router draws 11-12 watts of power with the wireless radios on and 7 with them off.

There's a little switch on the back to turn off all the blinking LEDs (the Power LED stays lit) which, I guess if you have this in your bedroom, could be useful and is a feature I have never seen before. There is also a button on the front to turn the radios on/off. I think I would rather use the built in scheduling to do that, but I'm sure there are those out there that will find this a useful feature.

This is an excellent router and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who has the cash. However, if you need something a little less spendy, the R7000 is also sublime and to be perfectly honest, even though the specs are better on paper for the R8000, I have yet to notice a significant performance difference between the 2--at least the way I use it. I suspect if we had higher wireless traffic on our network, I'd change my tune. However, the R7000 is also a fabulous router and at the time of this review, costs $110 less... which *is* a significant price difference. Take your pick.

I spend most of my time with the volume at a strong, but not really LOUD level and in this range the speakers are fantastic. Half of the time they play music, and the other half games and usual computer sound for YouTube and so on. They just sound super clean at any range short of really loud and for my lifestyle this is more important than a set that sound big and strong at specific volume levels.

My favorite part of these speakers it the mute (sound on-off) and volume wheel that also has an AUX/headphone ports. Words can't really do justice to the smooth and nice feel of the volume control and the tap on/off of the mute. No more reaching to a speaker to mess with the sound in an imprecise way. Sounds trivial, but once you have experience the tactile nature of the controls you will understand how great it is.

Promoting Bose is the last thing I expected to do, but these are a great set of speakers as a whole bundle if you don't need really loud, picture rattling base and presence.

title: One of the best point and shoots
text:
I had wanted this camera for a while and finally made the purchase when it was the deal of the day. I have owned many digital cameras, including the Panasonic DMC-ZS7. The LX5 is definitely an enthusiast's camera. It offers some of the easiest full manual controls I've seen on a point and shoot. There is a thumb dial on the rear of the camera that you can push in to adjust the exposure compensation. There is a slider switch on the side of the lens that allows you to switch between AF, Macro AF, and MF. The Macro AF is slightly slower than the standard AF, but it allows you to focus on subjects about 1cm from the lens. This allows for great close up shots of flowers, bugs, or other tiny things. I've used the manual focus a few times, which is quite easy to use, for a few shots on a tripod. The standard AF works quite well for normal shooting and is fast and accurate. There is also a manual switch on top of the lens which allows you to switch the aspect ratio which can be fun to play with. Image quality is quite impressive for a small camera. I typically shoot this camera in RAW and limit the ISO to 800. I'm a little picky with digital noise in the photos and try to keep the camera under ISO400. I feel images are usable up to 800, but don't like to push it over that. The RAW files that come out of this camera are amazing at low ISO and are very close to entry level dSLR cameras. The JPG files are the best I've seen in a point and shoot and offer some cool effects you can choose including miniature effect. I would say the images are noticeably better than the ZS7 which I think does quite well among other pocketable cameras. The LX5 is the first point and shoot i've used since really getting into photography that I've been surprised and impressed with the image quality. It does have the advantage of a larger image sensor which helps a lot with image quality. I primarily shoot a Canon 5D, but this camera is surprisingly convenient and a nice companion to a DSLR. I would recommend this to someone looking for a more advanced point and shoot.

PROS
excellent image quality
fast lens
fast autofocus
small size, though slightly too large to put in your pocket
wide angle lens

Cons
the lens cap is not built in (not a huge issue, but slightly inconvenient)
in full auto, the flash does not automatically pop up. you need to pop it up manually in order for it to be on. this is not a problem for me, but when you hand the camera to someone who is not familiar with cameras, this can be a problem.

Wish List
Larger image sensor (maybe micro 4/3)
Even better ISO performance

title: DESCRIPTION IS WRONG.
text: Per my conversation with the manufacturer, this antenna is NOT amplified. It does NOT have 36 DB gain. It does NOT have a 15-18 db gain as indicated on the manufacturer web site. It only has 5 db gain without amplifier and 25 db potential gain with amplifier, as indicated in the installation guide. It does NOT have an internal rotor motor. The available (on the manufacturer web site) amplifier is sold separately. Also, there are other good amplifiers in the market. The manufacturer admits an error on his web site. I tried to advise one seller but he refuses to change his description or contact the manufacturer. I live in a flat area. Transmitters are 25-50 miles away. You must extend the rod antennas and use an amplifier for best reception. This antenna is omnidirectional and will pick up some stations without an amplifier. My rating is for the antenna without amplifier. I tried it with an RCA amplifier (available on Amazon). It requires an additional piece of coax cable besides the one provided or a female to female joiner (available at Radio Shack). The antenna has a short piece of coax with a male end and this amplifier has a male end to be attached to the antenna. Although I have opted to purchase a better amplifier elsewhere, I would rate the antenna with an amplifier at 5 stars.

title: Affordable 3-in-1 Lighting Solution
text:
I wasn't sure what I was in for when I purchased this (there were no reviews yet), but I figured it was worth a shot given the price and the fact that it included a honeycomb grid. I'd already purchased the similarly priced Neewer 24 x 24" softbox and was extremely happy with it, but I also wanted something that produced less light spill, for more precise lighting, so the grid on this was a major selling point.

The product arrived very quickly, packed well in a long cardboard box. All the pieces--umbrella, diffuser, and honeycomb--came inside a nylon case with a velcro flap. A fairly flimsy case, mind you, but it does the job of keeping everything contained. The umbrella itself--with its reflective silver interior and zippered opening for a light stand--is better made, while the diffuser and grid fit the unit perfectly and do the job they're supposed to. Your light stand, flash, and hotshoe bracket all fit through the zippered hole and are positioned so the flash can bounce off the reflective surface. It seems a bit cramped in there (esp. with a large flash), and the ability to point the unit at a downward angle appears limited, but otherwise everything works extremely well. The results of using the grid were impressive, keeping the soft, diffused light from spilling onto the wall behind my subject.

The build quality isn't exactly rugged--if you're a working pro whose equipment takes regular abuse on location, the umbrella's ribs may not last long. But as a portable softbox for moderate studio use, it should be more than adequate, especially considering the price. With its ability to offer 3 different types of reflected light--bare, diffused, and with grid (4, if you use the grid without diffusion)--it really is a great option for those on a budget or anyone wanting to experiment with more sophisticated lighting techniques before moving up to heavier-duty gear. Just be sure you have a flash bracket that holds an umbrella, since one isn't included (there are a ton of them out there, most for under ten bucks).

Again, for the money, this unit really delivers. I'll be sure to post an update if it prematurely breaks or ends up lasting longer than exptected.

UPDATE JANUARY 21, 2013:
Well, it turns out the ribs were even less rugged than I thought--so I've deducted a star since my initial writeup. After only three (very light) uses, one of the top ribs bent, and on the 4th use another one did the same. I'm not happy about that, but for so little money I guess that's what you can expect. Am still using it in its disabled state, but I'll need to figure out a way to reinforce those ribs before the whole thing collapses. So, be very gentle with this umbrella--or else. You have been warned!

title: Toshiba E55 - no mouse buttons on touch pad, just a single slab
text:
I bought a Toshiba E55 at Best Buy because I wanted wireless 802.11 AC back in February. The touch pad looks identical to the touchpad in the E55 photo here - a single slab.
All my other 4 laptops in my family have a button for left click, a button for right click and the touchpad. So three surfaces.
This E55 is now going in for service a THIRD time because the computer thinks the left mouse (part of the slab) is clicked. Point is I can slide the mouse pointer around and the computer thinks there was a click when there wasn't. Perhaps 20 time per hour.
I am not leaning on it. I am not pushing on it. When you do push down on the bottom left corner of the slab, you hear an audible click. You had the tactile feel of a click. But none of that for these "ghost" clicks. The repair notes say both times that the problem was replicated and that they fixed it. All I can say is that I take it out of the shipping box and it is not fixed. I'm beginning to think this single slab is a design flaw.
Also, when it came back from service, the backlit keyboard no longer works, the shiny bezel around the screen has vertical scratched lines on both sides, about 4 inches long about 1/2 inch from the outside edge. There is also some gouging of the bezel in the bottom right corner. Also the Intel sticker to the left of the touchpad was first torn off and then left barely hanging.
Even more frustrating is the Toshiba repair call center. For the most part, they got adequate training in our version of English. But try to fathom this. The computer comes back from service in a box. I call to get it repaired a 2nd and now 3rd time, but this perfectly good box I have in hand can't be used again, I have to wait 3-5 business days for another box? We know how Amazon let's us just print a prepaid label immediately to send things back, but Toshiba not only is wasteful, but make us wait that extra time just to send it in. Because I bought at Best Buy, I couldn't return it after 17 days as a typical buyer. My fault there. When sold and shipped by Amazon you get 30 days to exchange.
What's also frustrating about Best Buy is looking at MOST of their 1 or 2 star reviews it is transparent that there are trolls who go through and mark these reviews "Not Helpful" simply because they had criticism of the product.
Next time I will wait for the features I want to be available on Amazon, and sold by Amazon.

title: I Am Difficult to Please, and This iPad Mini Case is a Total Winner
text:
I have owned this case now for several weeks, after having researched just about every iPad mini case I could find on the market. If you're like me and need to feel convinced before committing to a purchase, this is why I chose the ZaggKey Folio. I chose to purchase the iPad mini version of the case, but I believe they also make it for the larger-sized iPads.

- I am a touch-typist and appreciate the decent-sized keyboard on the ZaggKeys Folio. Compared to almost every other iPad mini case on the market (except for the ZaggKeys Cover, which has the identical keyboard) the ZaggKeys keyboard is one of the most large and comfortable. It also includes a row of native iPad function buttons, such as home, lock, volume, and other function keys.

- The overall size and form factor of the iPad without a case is appealing to me, and I wanted to preserve as much of that feeling within a case as possible. The ZaggKeys Folio is a thin design and lightweight case, and does not feel bulky.

- Some iPad cases use a flap or stand to hold the iPad upright, which limits the range in potential viewing angles. The ZaggKeys Folio holds the iPad just like a laptop so the screen can be adjusted forward and backward. It also has no problem holding the screen in place, as the hinge is very strong. Just yesterday I was working on my iPad in a room where light coming from behind me caused a glare that was quickly fixed by tilting the screen a bit.

- The iPad mini snaps into the ZaggKeys Folio case so that the keyboard folds against the iPad screen, and a cover protects the back of the iPad from scratches and impact damage. The fact that the case protects the back of the iPad is ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL to me in a case. As a side note, the ZaggKeys Cover is also a great case, but has no protection for the back of the iPad. Otherwise the cases are basically the same.

- A feature that didn't seem essential at first, but is now MUCH appreciated is the ZaggKeys Folio backlit keyboard. Using the keyboard case while in bed, a dark room, or being able to work while on a plane is comfortable and convenient. It has three brightness settings, and a pretty wide range of different colors for the backlight to choose from as well.

- The battery life on this keyboard is pretty insane. It is supposed to last for months when being used for hours a day (not considering the backlit keys power usage), and even while using the backlit keyboard the battery will last for weeks. It also has a battery indicator so you can feel confident about its power level, and the battery has no "memory" (meaning that you can recharge it while the battery is already partially charged and it won't hurt the long-term battery life). Another nice feature is that the keyboard goes into a standby mode while not in use for a little while, but wakes up instantly as soon as you go to use it again.

- A feature that does not bother me, but could be worth mentioning is that this case is designed to hold the iPad in landscape (horizontal) orientation. I don't often NEED to have my iPad in portrait orientation, but when I do simply holding the case sideways works fine. The iPad can also be quickly and easily removed from the case for use in portrait mode (perhaps for reading).

All in all, I am a picky person, spent a considerable amount of time researching the best iPad cases available, and this is my choice.

title: I'm quite dissapointed with it but...

First off, I got this since its the same brand as the Eclipse cleaning solution. And this is my first sensor loupe and the first time I have to clean my own sensor since previously, I was using cameras with highly effective sensor cleaning.

I have both a Nikon D3 and Nikon D700. The Nikon D3 sees a lot of action while the D700 is relative new in my inventory and has not seen much action either. When I first used the loupe on my Nikon D700, I cannot make heads or tails. It says that there are something like rubber feet to help hold the loupe securely. And the promo picture shows a 5D which means it should work with full frame cameras without issue. I have a hard time getting it to fit, in fact, I can't fit it at all. It stands on its own nicely, but my idea is that it should fit snugly like how the lens would fit onto the body.

Next is the magnification itself. 5X is fine, but I can't focus anything. It supposedly can rotate to focus but when I rotate until the whole thing pops out, I can't get my sensor in focus, I can get the front of the chamber in focus though.

Since this is my first sensor loupe, I have no idea if its supposed to be working like this or not. I can see dust, but it has to be pretty big and its blur. But when I swing the glass away, I can see the dust on my sensor perfectly fine. Making this pretty much an expensive sensor ring light. I'm not sure if it means that only big dust can be viewed albeit out of focus. And my D3 recently was cleaned by Nikon and now I only have 3 dust spots which is not really visible at f11 which is the usual max I would shoot at. I will update this review when I have something to update.

title: Fix to make them LAST MUCH LONGER
text:
Westone NOTE: These Shure tips are the same tips included in the tip pack with Westone 4 earphones. You only get 1 pair in the Westone pack and they do not offer a replacement for just these tips. You must pay over $20 for the pack and you only get a single set of these tips.

REVIEW:

These tips worked better for me than any of the other style tips I've tried. But don't be fooled by reviews; ALL EARS ARE DIFFERENT!!! Try them all and use what works for you. If this style works best, USE IT!

As a triple flange tip goes this tip has pros and cons.

Pros: The stem on this tip is longer than most tips which gives you the ability to push it deeper into the ear canal if you need to. Also, the stem opening is smaller than most so it fits much tighter on the earphone's stem making it less likely to come off the earphone and stay lodged in your ear when you try to take them out of your ears.

Cons: Being a stiffer rubber than some of the other tips, it tends to have more of a 'memory' and starts to retain the shape of the ear canal fairly quickly. Over time, this memory prevents the tip from 'spreading out' and it therefore loses the sealing ability that it had.

FIX: I decided to try something after each use and I have gotten spectacular results. After each use (used for in-ear monitors during rehearsals and shows), I wash them and then flip the large and middle flange up and leave it until the next use. This resets the memory they tend to develop and even spreads the flange out a little more. I get an even better seal after using this method than I did on the brand new pair! They are lasting a long time now--four months and still sealing tight!

title: Seeing the believing!
text:
While the unit has "great reviews" from others, it get's one star from a Video Game Industry professional as it's the lowest rating available. Where to start... The projector is unable to display a fully focused image across the screen - perhaps 60% of the image will be in focus at the most. Running tests for accurate pixel-perfect display, it failed every test. Don't let "FAST" display mode fool you, it's marketing lingo for a low-resolution image that it scaled to a 1080P display. There are other words that come to mind when describing the image quality this mode produces. "FINE" mode delivers a muddy image at best, when compared to LCD projectors from 2006 and today's DLP offerings. The low-cost bulb replacement at $99 was another factor that influenced my initial selection of this device. In retrospect, it could come with a FREE and unlimited bulb policy and I still would not use it in my theatre.

Now.. If you don't care about image clarity / quality and are looking for a projector with long lamp life. This is a great choice, if you can get past the overly loud fan that even in ECO mode is overpowering.

title: Not "worth" it, simple as that...
text:
UPDATE 08/28/2014:

This router is going back to the store. For the past few ays I have had nightmare with this router on its 2.4Ghz network. My laptop and other mobile devices connected to 2.4Ghz network lose network connection as soon as it reconnects. Only way to get back online is to disable wifi on the devices and turn it back on. I have degraded my ratings from 2 to 1 star as that is the least allowed rating. Absolutely worthless expensive piece of equipment I ever owned. This is my first and last netgear wireless router.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I picked up this from my local other store so you will not see "amazon verified purchase" stamp on this review.

I bought this router to replace my perfectly working Asus RT-66R model. I wanted to change my router just to get bit more range in my new 2200sqft home. Prior to getting this router I have tried one of the best range extender Ampedwireless AE-20. It's range was excellent, but connection was very much degraded and struggled to get connected at times though it was set up to clone settings from original router.

So, after reading few positive reviews on BBY and mixed reviews on amazon, I decided to give new Nighthawk R8000 a try. I am happy with its slightly improved range than Asus and very much disappointed with its 2.4Ghz performance. I have more than 15 years of network experience and I really don't bother tech support unless until it is really out of my hand and hardware specific.

Here I am trying to do a fair comparison with two routers I have (Asus & Netgear) + sign means "better" and - signs means "poor"

Wired Connection:
+ RT-66R has excellent wired connection which works at par with Motorola SB6141's consistency

- R8000 has fair wired connection with slight consistency issues.

Wireless 5.0 Ghz:
+ RT-66R has excellent consistent connection
+ R8000 has excellent consistent connection as well at full speed by ISP

Wireless 5.0 Ghz Second Connection:
- RT-66R Not applicable (does not come with this feature)
+ R8000 excellent connection with full speed by ISP's

Wireless 2.4 Ghz:
+RT-66R has excellent connection with 80~Mbps out of my actual 120~Mbps ISP feed at channel 6 with 450 Mbps capability.

- R8000 is a complete failure in terms of 2.4Gh network
I have tried all available channels and found it degrade my 120~Mbps connection 1-14 ~ Mbps

At this point I called customer service and it sounded like they kind of aware of the issue. With minimal trouble shooting and changing the channels to their recommended channels (01, 06, 09 & 11), there was no improvement. So they asked me to degrade from 600Mpbs to 289Mbps and it started working.

So technically now their claim of 3200Mbps became 2911Mbps.

Access Control:
+ RT-66R has fairly good access control capabilities. You can schedule what time of the day each device can access the internet. This feature is important for me as I found it is very useful with kids on top of parental control settings.

- R8000 access control only let you allow or deny connecting a particular device. You cannot decide what time it should be able to connect. - Major drawback for me.

Parental Control:

- RT-66R has poor parental control settings, but with an option to point DNS to OpenDNS we can achieve better parental control settings with their FREE offerings.

+R8000 - also use OpenDNS but with dedicated service assigned to netgear so that you can add bypass account also which can't be done with OpenDNS free account. This is the only additional benefit I found with this router so far compared to RT-66R.

VPN:
+ RT-66R is also able to use OpenVPN with mobile access with their free App. I was abe to access local network using iOS and Android devices with no issues.

-R8000 - did not bother to check as soon as I read that it does not support mobile devices using same OpenVPN platform.

LED Control:
- RT-66R - Not applicable (missing feature)

+R8000 - very useful feature if you have your router in bedroom or other place you don't like lot of flashing lights. Can be accessed via web GUI and with a dedicated hard button at the rear of the router.

USB Storage and Cloud access:
+RT-66R allow you to create a personal cloud with your router with AiCloud application. I am able to enjoy my music and movies over AiCloud on the move.

- R8000 - could not find any documentation about cloud access. Only information I found is about ReadyCloud and it is dedicated to Netgear NAS only. Another major setback for an expensive router.

Web GUI:
Though Netgear has a simple interface and easy to follow GUI, it lack modern look and feeling. I like Asus GUI better.

Customer service:
+ Asus- Never had to call them. No subscription fee, 24/7 free support (as far as you are within product warranty).

- Netgear - Though I received prompt customer service when I called, it was shocking to learn that the phone support is only available for 90 days of purchase, then you have to pay PREMIUM subscription to get phone support.

CONCLUSION:

I have thoroughly tested all important feature that I need. Rest of the features are generic to me and I am not bothered much about them.

I am sure this router with Dual 5.0Ghz network will be very useful for those who have new wireless devices. For me I have a lot of devices that depends on 2.4Ghz frequency such as smoke detectors, thermostat, laptop that connects to NAS for backup etc. and degraded and unreliable 2.4Ghz network make it absolutely worthless considering the amount I spent on this router.

I am seriously thinking to take this back to the store. I don't see any point in spending almost double amount of money to get a couple of benefits and a lot of drawbacks and pay for a premium to get their phone support if needed to an overpriced product.

I would not recommend this router at its current price and it is unable to meet its original claims and comes with a premium phone support after 90 days.

title: Great units for the price.
text:
I have being using the Startech VGA extenders for event setup and installs for the last few years with great result. I have managed to push these 400 feet, with a cat5 coupler half-way along with acceptable results, which for the price is pretty impressive. Having the extra VGA outputs on each device is also useful, allowing you to connect a monitor to check the output of your VA source and/or connect to a second transmitter if you need to send to more sources. And at the receiver end you can connect two displays easily. Audio works well, and I have used the units to feed a laptop from a stage to video/audio control numerous times with no issues with the laptop detecting the device. The units really are very forgiving, even when run over cheap cat 5 or next to other wiring, BUT you have to check the signal boost switch on the receiver to make sure you get the best results. I have also used the transmitter with the two cat 5 outputs and the cat 5 repeater units successfully. The repeater unit is great when running two projectors as you can loop through from the first projector.

These are definitely superior to unpowered passive extenders, which often require a shielded cat 5 to work correctly.

title: Multi-coated CPL for a low cost

I brought 5 AGFA filters for 3 Canon lenses, 52mm, 58mm and 77mm. When I got the filters, I took numerous test shots with all the lenses and filter combinations. Overall, they were stored in a nice case, clear (did not dim) and multicoated (purple hue, like expensive eyeglasses). The threads are ok, but just have to remember not to over-tighten. I am very happy with the AGFA's UV filters (I gave it 5-stars on its product review page); they exceeded my expectations in value. However the CPLs were not the same. On the 58mm CPL, the ring did not turn smoothly and felt a bit loose. The 77mm CPL ring did turn smoothly but it has a speck or two of imperfections visible during close examination. Luckily, the specks did not show in the pictures. Overall, for its price and the fact that the CPL works well enough, I am going to just keep it. Sure I can buy other brand name CPLs (one single piece of glass) that cost almost as much as a nice camera lenses (with its complexity AF, motor and lens elements). But I rather spend my money on something of value like more nice camera lenses. The UV filters were good investment to protect my lenses with either Improved or no negative visible effects. The CPLs, despite its flaws, they work. I could turn the ring to adjust the "CPL effects," from light to dark to blackout and see its effects immediately. With a turn of the ring, the blue sky turned from pale to light blue to intense blue. Also, the CPLs did not darken my pictures noticeably (vs UV filter vs no filter).
